POSITION SPECIFICS​

The Cancer Institute at the Penn State College of Medicine in Hershey, PA is seeking a Human Research Technologist.


This position executes clinical research protocols; tasks may include (but are not limited to) recruiting/consenting/assessing/following patients, obtaining biospecimen samples, creating/maintaining records, collecting/transmitting data, troubleshooting minor-to-moderate protocol/compliance issues, meeting and regularly informing PI including writing reports and ppt presentations. This is an entry level position and this person will focus on straightforward studies with supervision from higher level CRC's and research nurses.

- Managing documentation and data collection needs for the investigator(s), sponsor(s), CTO office, and other stakeholders, both on campus (e.g. internal monitors/auditors) and off campus (e.g. FDA). Compared to HRT-intermediate professional, the HRT-advanced professional will take the lead on more complex, higher risk protocols.

- Work on a clinical trial research project portfolio by screening, recruiting and assessing subjects for clinical trials, managing the patient's schedule of activities, recording and communicating this and other information. Works closely with research nurse and CRC(s) on these procedures.

- Work with biospecimens from study patients, including procurement, basic lab techniques (e.g. centrifuging), transmission to/from laboratories, preparation for transmission of specimens to appropriate location(s), recording and maintaining data related to specimens.

- Coordinate workflow within study team and with sponsors and investigators to ensure proper management of trial activity. Coordination of meetings including preparation of reports/slides for meetings. Compile information from meetings, particularly action items, and communicate them to stakeholders.

- Documentation of study specific workload/activities and compile study records for proper, compliant invoicing.

description:
Job Description

An opportunity has arisen for the position of Senior Manufacturing Biotech Associate at our single-use Dunboyne facility.


As Senior Biotech Associate you will be part of a self-directed work team in Solution Prep Operations, responsible for all procedures and processes associated with the manufacture of Drug Substance.

Ability to work 24/5 shift operations, which include days, nights and in rotation is required.


This role is a site-based role.


Bring energy, knowledge, innovation to carry out the following:

  • As a senior team member, be strong technically, with an excellent grasp of processes and procedures. Already an SME on many processes, be strongly motivated to acquire knowledge and understand all Downstream processes to a micro level
  • Proactively train, coach and mentor less experienced team members, by being approachable, supportive, inclusive and generous with knowledge, while striving to work in a cohesive and proactive team, with a ‘never let a teammate fail’ mindset
  • Display flexibility, adaptability, innovation, with a reflexive ability to think on your feet, also possess a strong skill set for logical root cause analysis, and problem solving
  • Be able to organise and lead local work teams, also deliver business unit goals through strong and cohesive collaboration with other departments, within a matrix reporting environment
  • Display high initiative and be ready to take responsibility; thinks ahead, seeks the production schedule daily, organises local work teams and lays plans to achieve or exceed the schedule
  • Takes part in shift handovers and Tier meetings, raising concerns or issues promptly and providing options for resolutions.
  • Be actively involved by participating in inspections, GEMBA’s and Go-See’s, OPPS, improvement projects and other MPS initiatives
  • Perform EBR and documentation reviews, QN investigation and closure, and any other documentation or administrative tasks as directed by your manager
  • Utilise Lean Six Sigma Tools to support the initiative of continuous improvement (CI)
  • Be proficient to SME level with production systems such as MES, DeltaV, SAP, GLIMS, PROCAL and others
  • Deputised when required, to represent the department at meetings and discussions, and performs any other duties as appropriate when assigned by the Manager

What skills you will need:

In order to excel in this role, you will more than likely have:

  • A Level 7, or higher, qualification in a science or engineering discipline, with a minimum of 3 years’ experience in a GMP regulated Manufacturing environment.
  • Strong experience in a highly regulated pharmaceutical manufacturing environment
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to work in a cross functional collaborative team
  • Possess a detailed overview of the overall Upstream and Downstream processes, with particular expertise and working knowledge of the Downstream manufacturing process
  • Maintain a high level of expertise and working knowledge of the process equipment.
  • A proven ability to work with automated systems such as Manufacturing Execution System (MES), Systems Applications and Products (SAP), Delta V etc.
  • Strong knowledge and understanding of manufacturing GMP and quality systems
  • Demonstrate troubleshooting and problem-solving competency
  • Desire to learn and develop. Ability to interact with multiple stakeholders across numerous departments
  • Knowledge and experience of Kanban, JIT, 5S and Lean Manufacturing methodologies
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and know when to escalate issues for resolution.
  • Excellent trouble shooting skills as an ability to coach and mentor self-directed teams through complex problem solving. High degree of problem-solving ability and adherence to scheduled timelines.
  • A proven ability to deliver on tight timelines

Our facility in Dunboyne joined our network in September 2020. Our Dunboyne site is our Company’s first Biologics Drug Substance Single Use Commercialisation Facility, playing an important role in helping to commercialise key medicines. The cutting-edge innovation and collaboration between our Company’s research and manufacturing teams will significantly accelerate the time it takes to bring a medicine to market for the benefit of patients around the world.

We keep the patient at the very heart of all that we do and strive to find solutions and treatments for some of the world's most challenging healthcare needs.


As an equal opportunity employer, we are proud to be a company that embraces the value of bringing talented and committed people together.


Please don't hesitate to contact the Talent Acquisition Advisor assigned to this role should you need any support during our recruitment process.

We are committed to flexible working where possible, and this is why our Company has introduced a new hybrid working model for office-based colleagues around the world.


Please feel free to speak to us about what flexibility means to you during your application.


So, if you are ready to:

Invent solutions to meet unmet healthcare needs, please apply today.

Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing, Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing, Biotechnology, CNC Operations, Computer Literacy, Data Analysis, FDA Regulations, Flexibility Training, Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), Industrial Manufacturing, Information Systems, Kanban, Laboratory Techniques, Manufacturing, Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), Manufacturing Processes, Manufacturing Quality Control, Master Batch Records, Material Selection, Matrix Management, Multidisciplinary Teamwork, Pharmaceutical Manufacturing, Pharmaceutical Process Development, Problem Solving, Process Equipment {+ 9 more}

description:
About GF

GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors that enable AI at scale, from the cloud to the physical world. We partner closely with our customers to deliver differentiated, power-efficient, high-performance solutions for high-growth markets. Across our global footprint in the United States, Europe and Asia, our teams are solving complex challenges that shape the future of technology. At GF, you'll find the opportunity to make an impact, work with world-class talent and contribute to a more secure, sustainable future.


Summary of Role

GlobalFoundries Fab 1 in Dresden Germany is looking for a motivated and skilled experienced engineer to be a part of the Customer Engineering team. The primary responsibility in this role would be to work with customers to plan for their New Products in Fab1, align internally and run customer meetings where multiple technical items are discussed. A responsibility is also to track and move wafers across sites, OSATs to ship to our customers.


Your Job

Perform as technical conduit for Customer Programs from Customer Prototyping (NPI) to Product EOL

  • Act as primary Engineering channel ensuring crisp & clear communication.
  • Be the focal point for Customer communication to the Fab, aligning messaging internally and then sharing externally with the customer.
  • Work with the Fab1 Production Control, Planning and Product Integration to track internal dates and On Time Delivery (OTD) metrics.
  • Run customer meetings, ensuring action items are aligned and followed up.
  • Take ownership and drive any issue for the customer project to a solution, involving all required departments.
  • Interface with Account Managers (AM), Field Application Engineering (FAE), all sales teams and Customers to enable program success.
  • Achieve revenue goals and derive customer satisfaction.

Required Qualifications

  • Education: 4 Year Technical / Bachelor/Master Degree in Science, Math, Engineering or Semiconductor Manufacturing.
  • Extensive experience in manufacturing or customer facing engineering role.
  • Proven track record of leading cross‑functional collaboration, driving alignment across diverse engineering teams, and influencing stakeholders at multiple levels.
  • Strong organizational skills with a focus on efficiency and accuracy.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills; fosters positive working relationships.
  • Capable of managing multiple tasks and prioritizing activities under pressure.
  • Fluency in English Language – written & verbal (C1).

We Offer

The position is open-ended and to be filled as soon as possible.

13th month salary, bonus payments, assistance with relocation to Dresden.

Family friendly part-time models, trust flextime, salary conversion into free time

Career stages for every job, internal qualification offers, promotion of external educational qualifications

On-site gym and beach volleyball court, bike leasing, subsidized employee restaurant

Cooperation at eye level - everyone is on first name terms with us, budget for individual team events, social commitment via GlobalGives

title: Product Manager
location: Tel Aviv-Yafo, Tel Aviv District, Israel
description:
About REAL

REAL is building an AI Execution Platform for enterprise real estate organizations.

Our platform transforms fragmented business and financial data into connected intelligence, enabling customers to automate complex workflows, improve operational accuracy, and make better business decisions.

At REAL, you’ll work with cutting-edge AI technology, enterprise customers, and a product that is redefining how CRE organizations operate.

REAL Values

  • Ownership: We take responsibility and move decisively.
  • Clarity: We simplify complexity to deliver meaningful impact.
  • Accuracy: Precision matters in everything we build.
  • Velocity: We work with urgency and intent.
  • Partnership: We collaborate closely with customers and teammates.

Role Overview

We’re looking for a Product Manager who loves solving complex problems, building intuitive products, and turning cutting-edge AI capabilities into real business value.

At REAL, you’ll work at the intersection of AI, data, user experience, and enterprise real estate, lease and accounting, construction & architecture, and facilities, shaping how some of the world’s largest organizations interact with their data and execute critical business workflows.

This is a highly hands-on role with real ownership and impact. You’ll lead product features end-to-end, work directly with customers to understand their challenges, and collaborate closely with engineering and design to turn complex requirements into simple, powerful product experiences.

We’re looking for someone who brings a strong foundation in at least one of three areas: data-intensive products, UX-driven product development, or deep industry knowledge in commercial real estate (CRE) / PropTech.

You should know the CRE market. What matters most is how fast you learn: you pick up new domains quickly, ask the right questions, and turn what you learn into a product.

What You’ll Do

  • • Own product features end-to-end – from discovery and problem definition through design, development, launch, and continuous improvement, balancing speed and quality in a fast-paced, iterative environment.
  • • Turn complex customer workflows into intuitive solutions – understand business processes, data structures, and customer needs, translating them into clear, scalable product experiences.
  • • Lead proactive product discovery – engage directly with customers and prospects through user interviews, validation, outbound outreach, and ongoing conversations to identify needs and new opportunities.
  • • Leverage AI tools and technologies – build AI-powered product experiences and use AI tools for prototyping, research, and faster product development.
  • • Collaborate closely with design and engineering – define user journeys, detailed product requirements, business logic, edge cases, and system behavior, using prototypes to bring ideas to life.
  • • Make data-driven product decisions – analyze product usage, customer feedback, and industry insights to prioritize improvements and deliver measurable impact.

Requirements

What We’re Looking For

  • 3–5 years of experience in Product Management, preferably in a B2B, SaaS, or enterprise technology environment, or in industries related to architecture, construction, real estate, or design.
  • Strong expertise in the following areas:
    • Bringing product vision to execution
    • Data & Analytics: Experience with data-intensive products, complex datasets, analytics, or data-driven workflows.
    • CRE / PropTech: Hands-on background in the real estate world: enterprise real estate, lease and accounting, construction, architecture, engineering, facilities. You understand how they run day to day.
    • UX & Product Experience: Strong UX orientation and ability to design intuitive user journeys and simplify complex interactions.
  • Strong AI and data-driven orientation – a must. Hands-on experience with AI tools, product analytics platforms (Mixpanel, Heap, or similar), and prototyping tools (Figma, v0, Lovable, or similar).
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to understand complex customer workflows and translate business needs into clear break down complex systems into clear product logic
  • Customer-centric and collaborative mindset, with experience working directly with customers, engineering, and design teams.
  • Strong ownership and execution skills, high attention to detail, and excellent English communication skills.

title: Senior Manager, Supplier Quality & Development
description:
Work Model: You’ll work in a hybrid model, onsite at your designated Regal Rexnord location, with flexibility to work remotely.

____________________


POSITION SUMMARY

This is an on-site hybrid role based out of Pune or Hyderabad.

This position reports to Director of Supply Chain India region and is responsible for supplier selection and development. It is a management role with three direct reports of supplier quality development engineers. This position will provide regional quality leadership in assessing supplier capabilities, achieving cost saving projects by qualifying new parts and new suppliers, contributing to regional category strategy and managing supplier performances. This role works closely with segment, global category teams, divisional product leaders, operations and other key stakeholders to deploy strategies that drive value and sustainability in our supply chain. This key role will manage supplier related quality issues in regional plants and export based suppliers to drive overall supplier performance across Regal Rexnord.

RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Supplier Selection and Auditing:

• Lead supplier selection during design and development phases

• Develop and prioritize auditing schedules to ensure regular supplier audits

• Act as the supplier quality representative on design and development teams

• Conduct Supplier Scorecard reviews to assess suppliers' ability to meet quality, delivery, and service targets

• Conduct supplier audits and ensure timely closure of corrective actions

2. Cost Saving Projects and Project Management:

• Take an active role in Cost Saving projects to achieve best value for the company

• Assign proper resources to support all projects and ensure the performance of supplier is sufficient to

achieve saving goals while aligning the same direction with long term supplier strategies with category

managers

• Serve as the key interface between suppliers and internal stakeholders for all issues to meet the project

schedule with focus on qualification process and requirements

3. Compliance and Improvement:

• Audit and evaluate suppliers' internal processes for compliance with organizational, customer, and

regulatory requirements

• Maintain regular contact and communication with suppliers, including site visits

• Ensure suppliers develop effective corrective actions for quality and delivery problems

• Support product transfers to contract manufacturing sites and participate in developing required Quality

Plans and protocols

4. Performance Monitoring:

• Monitor and report on operational performance at both the subcontract and individual supplier levels.

• Track supplier performance on schedule and quality metrics

• Hold periodic meetings with the plant based Supplier Quality Manager and Category Managers to hold

supplier accountable for quality improvement

• Ensure proper control plans are in place for changes in parts and supplier processes

• Ensure effectiveness of supplier root cause analysis and corrective actions

QUALIFICATIONS

1. Education:

• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering.

2. Experience:

• 15+ years of experience in Supplier Quality Engineering.

• 5+ years managerial experience or/and quality management in leading supplier quality teams, quality

system management or project managements.

• Willingness to travel domestically up to 60%;

3. Technical Skills:

• Hands-on exposure to quality system requirements of AS9100 or ISO 9001.

• Understanding of basic quality tools such as PFA, PPAP, Process capability, FMEAs, and control plans.

• Extensive knowledge of machining or metal processing techniques.

• Proven success in the use and mentoring of Problem-Solving methods, Root Cause analysis and Statistical

decision-making including application knowledge of Minitab.

• Strong analytical skills with the ability to thoroughly analyze, interpret data / information to make sound

informed decisions.

4. Certifications, preferred:

• Certified ASQ Quality Engineer

• Six Sigma Green Belt or higher


About Regal Rexnord


Regal Rexnord is a publicly held global industrial manufacturer with 30,000 associates around the world who help create a better tomorrow by providing sustainable solutions that power, transmit and control motion. The Company’s electric motors and air moving subsystems provide the power to create motion. A portfolio of highly engineered power transmission components and subsystems efficiently transmits motion to power industrial applications. The Company’s automation offering, comprised of controls, actuators, drives, and precision motors, controls motion in applications ranging from factory automation to precision control in surgical tools.


The Company’s end markets benefit from meaningful secular demand tailwinds, and include factory automation, food & beverage, aerospace, medical, data center, warehouse, alternative energy, residential and commercial buildings, general industrial, construction, metals and mining, and agriculture.


Regal Rexnord is comprised of three operating segments: Industrial Powertrain Solutions, Power Efficiency Solutions, and Automation & Motion Control. Regal Rexnord has offices and manufacturing, sales and service facilities worldwide. For more information, including a copy of our Sustainability Report, visit RegalRexnord.com.

You'll develop ML models that detect opportunities, diagnose performance issues, and recommend actions—then embed these insights into AI agents, dashboards, and GenAI-powered tools used by sales teams.

We have 8,000 employees in a network of 55 offices across the Nordics united by our values: collaboration, innovation, pride, and passion for our work. And safety and sustainability are embedded in everything that we do.

The Nordic Corporate Real Estate team is primarily accountable for managing the working environment across WSP’s Nordic real estate portfolio.

The main focus of the CRE Team is to ensure WSP’s workplace serves to attract and retain the best talent within our industry by enabling our them to work productively and collaboratively in an enjoyable working environment.

ROLE
Reporting to the Director of Corporate Real Estate (EMEA & APAC), the Head of Workplace (Nordics) is responsible for the strategic development and operational management of WSP’s real estate portfolio across the Nordic region, comprising the following countries: Sweden, Finland and Norway.

The Nordic region represents comprises c.1m sq.ft. and 107 locations (65 offices and serviced offices) and annual operating costs of approximately CAD $62m.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES

  • To continually measure and assess the safety performance of all CRE managed activities and ensure safety remains paramount in the planning and execution of CRE operations with strict adherence to WSP H&S policies & regional legislation.

  • To develop and implement the regional real estate strategies ensuring alignment to global workplace objectives whilst serving the needs of the regional businesses.

  • To serve as the senior point of contact for all real estate activities (Nordics) establishing effective working relationships with regional senior managers and internal CRE departments accordingly.

  • To monitor future lease events to enable effective planning and timely decision making to ensure the estate is always performing optimally for the business.

  • In conjunction with WSP real estate advisors, lead on all real estate transactions and associated negotiations ensuring commercial optimisation (e.g. lease renewals, acquisitions, disposals, dilapidations, rent reviews, etc.).

  • To routinely liaise with regional business unit leaders on their future workspace requirements to help inform the real estate strategy.

  • To facilitate close collaboration between the CRE, Project and FM workstreams to deliver high quality and cost-effective services alongside partnering functions such as IT, Procurement, Finance.

  • To undertake feasibility studies and cost benefit analysis to support the strategic decision making.

  • To develop detailed business cases / investment proposals for Executive approval.

  • To implement systems to monitor occupancy and utilisation levels across WSP’s real estate assets to help inform future decision making.

  • To co-ordinate and undertake workplace surveys to assess current performance and future service requirements.

  • To actively contribute to the development of WSP’s workplace strategy, ensuring a working environment that retains and attracts the best talent in our industries whilst maintaining effective cost management and value to our business.

  • To maintain a knowledge of trends and best practices within the corporate real estate industry.

  • To identify, evaluate and implement workplace related initiatives that support WSP’s ESG strategic aspirations.

  • To develop and implement management policies and processes as required to ensure all real estate services are delivered to a high standard of operational efficiency and compliance with national legislation.

  • To prepare annual and interim opex and capex financial forecasts.

  • To monitor the financial performance the estate working closely with the Head of Performance to identify cost saving measures and inform future financial forecasting.

  • Develop and implement a rolling 5-year capital investment programme including the anticipated life cycle requirements of plant and equipment.

  • Undertake benchmarking exercises to establish performance against industry peers.

  • Ensure the CRE function is sufficiently prepared to respond to a crisis incidents supported by business continuity plans, policies and testing regimes.

  • When designated, to lead the CRE team in the event of a crisis / incident impacting business continuity.

KEY COMPETENCIES AND EXPERIENCE

  • Highly customer centric with excellent communications skills

  • Minimum 5 years experience leading the workplace strategy and delivery of real estate services across a European commercial office portfolio > 1m sq.ft.

  • Experience of leading commercial property transactions within a large private organisation.

  • Preferably multi-lingual (English + additional European language)

  • Detailed knowledge of the real estate / FM industry including best practices across Europe.

  • Analytical and financial skills necessary to develop and comprehend strategic plans and budgets.

  • Ability to manage through ambiguity and build a strong internal network.

  • Results-oriented with a desire to learn and support new technologies and processes.

  • Effective organizational skills with ability to delegate, prioritise and manage multiple projects under pressure.

  • Proficient with MS Word, MS Excel, MS Power Point

  • Strong communication skills, both written and oral.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Degree qualified (preferably within a real estate related discipline)

  • Membership of a relevant professional industry body (e.g. IWFM, MCIBSE, RICS)

  • Valid driver’s licence

CONTACT

Director of Corporate Real Estate (EMEA & APAC): Toby Chapman, toby.chapman@wsp.com
Recruitment/HR: Therese Galvez, therese.galvez@wsp.com

APPLICATION

We look forward to receiving your application, no later than 2026-12-10.

title: Vice President, EMEA Employee Compliance Advisory
description:
About this role

Your team


Employee Compliance sits within BlackRock's Legal & Compliance function and is responsible for the framework governing employees' personal activities. The EMEA Employee Compliance Advisory team provides practical advice and guidance on Employee Compliance requirements and supports the identification, assessment, and management of employee conflicts. The team operates within a globally consistent framework while providing regionally attuned engagement, local regulatory interpretation, and judgment-based review across EMEA.

Your role and impact


As Vice President, EMEA Employee Compliance Advisory, you will provide clear, practical, risk-based advice across the region, with a particular focus on personal trading, private investments, Outside Business Activities (OBA), and Gifts & Entertainment (G&E). You will manage complex, sensitive, and higher-risk matters while providing high-touch support to the EMEA executive population. You will apply sound judgment and discretion, help ensure advice and outcomes are consistent and well documented, and use insights from advisory activity to identify emerging risks and recurring themes that can strengthen the broader Employee Compliance program.

Your responsibilities


In every role at BlackRock, you'll be expected to apply sound judgement and critical thinking to solve complex problems, adapt as the business evolves, and combine the curiosity to explore new approaches and technologies with the rigor to challenge the results. The scope of this role also includes the following responsibilities:

  • Provide practical, risk-based Employee Compliance advice across EMEA, managing employee queries and submissions relating to personal trading, private investments, OBA, and G&E, and escalating novel or judgment-based matters appropriately.
  • Issue non-compliance notifications and support targeted OBA and G&E campaigns, training, and employee communications across the region.
  • Review policy exceptions, escalations, and pre-clearance requests across personal trading, private investments, OBA, and G&E, ensuring decisions and conditions are appropriately documented.
  • Provide high-touch support to the EMEA executive population and engage effectively with executive assistants, family offices, financial advisers, and brokers while maintaining appropriate policy standards and discretion.
  • Deliver training and communications for functions supporting executives and assist in resolving legacy records and data issues.
  • Operate the regional advisory hotline, support regulatory and audit activity, and contribute to regional training and local policy implementation.
  • Maintain connectivity with regional Chief Compliance Officers (CCOs) and partner across Program Operations, Advisory Compliance, Information Barriers/Control Room, Legal, and Human Resources, using advisory activity and case trends to inform policies, procedures, controls, training, and communications.

Your experience


  • Significant relevant experience in Compliance, Legal, Risk, or a related control function within financial services, ideally within asset management, investment management, or banking.
  • Strong subject-matter expertise in employee compliance and personal conflicts, including personal trading, private investments, Outside Business Activities (OBA), and Gifts & Entertainment (G&E).
  • Strong understanding of regulatory and conflicts-of-interest considerations relating to employees' personal activities, Codes of Ethics, and EMEA conduct and personal-account-dealing requirements.
  • Proven ability to assess complex, sensitive, and judgment-based matters, apply sound risk judgment, make well-reasoned decisions, and escalate appropriately.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to translate complex requirements into clear, practical guidance and constructively challenge stakeholders at different levels of the organization.
  • Experience working across compliance functions and centralized operations, combined with the discretion, organization, and relationship-management skills required to support senior executives and their representatives.
  • A bachelor's degree or equivalent experience; an advanced legal, compliance, or related professional qualification is advantageous. Experience with private markets or private-investment reviews would also be beneficial.

BlackRock’s hybrid work model is designed to enable a culture of collaboration and apprenticeship that enriches the experience of our employees, while supporting flexibility for all. We remain focused on increasing the impactful moments that arise when we work together in person – aligned with our commitment to performance and innovation. As a new joiner, you can count on this hybrid model to accelerate your learning and onboarding experience here at BlackRock.


Guidance on AI use for candidates

We encourage candidates to use AI thoughtfully to learn, prepare, and work more effectively; but during our interview process, we want to focus on getting to know you through your own experiences, thinking, and judgment. title: Manager, Data & Analytics Compliance, APAC
description:
Our global teams took on the challenge to make a difference in the way the global financial markets operate. Would you seek the same challenge?

At LSEG, we help our customers achieve success by providing access to an open platform that uncovers opportunity and catalyzes change.


Role Profile

The Manager, D&A Compliance –APAC is an established and existing role within the London Stock Exchange Group “LSEG”. The role will support the D&A Compliance team as a trusted business partner, providing salient guidance and advisory support to senior management within the D&A Business lines and to protect the LSEG brand, its products and employees.

Reporting to the Senior Manager in APAC, the Compliance Manager, APAC will lead all aspects of the compliance framework for the business across Asia-Pacific and provide compliance advice and support to meet evolving business development. This role will be responsible for ensuring appropriate policy, processes, systems and structures are in place to run compliance with the businesses legal and regulatory obligations in APAC. In particular, this role would primarily focus across the Asia-Pacific regulatory footprint of the business including but not limited to the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission (HKSFC), the Australian Securities and Investments Commission, and other relevant APAC financial regulators, plus a growing focus in markets such as China, Taiwan, India, Indonesia requiring compliance guidance. This role will also have a global nexus to support multi-jurisdictional projects and workstreams.

The Compliance Manager will be responsible for supporting the following activities:

  • Business Relationship: develop and maintain business division relationships across the D&A business within D&A as well as the wider LSE Group by providing timely and effective advice and developing the communication channels to ensure a two-way flow of information. Participation in regulatory projects that have a business impact, ensuring that changes are appropriately embedded in the business.
  • Regulatory relationship and reporting: support relationship management with relevant regulators across the globe, particularly APAC, including regulatory ad-hoc notifications, client communications, BAU correspondence, and periodic filings. Maintain relevant regulatory licenses within APAC and ensure all licensing requirements and obligations are met. Primary liaison with regulators including the Hong Kong SFC.
  • Analysis and advice: provide compliance advisory services, but also valuable challenge & scrutiny, whilst maintaining a “trusted business partner” relationship. Sign off on marketing materials and financial promotion materials to ensure it is in compliance with local laws and regulations.
  • Regulatory strategy and change: support regulatory change projects, to ensure that the design and implementation proposed by the Business addresses regulatory risks and obligations, including leading sub-workstreams where required. Provide input into regulatory horizon scanning, including drafting responses to consultations, and collaborating with other Compliance, Legal, Risk and Government Relations teams.
  • Governance and MI: prepare concise and effective MI / reports for and participate in various governance forums and committees, and be empowered to call out risks, issues, or concerns via senior colleagues and forums as appropriate. Ensure proper governance arrangements are adhered to.
  • Policies: Supporting the management of compliance policies and the policy governance. Develop, review, and update the suite of regulatory policies and procedures, including providing input into business processes. design, implement and improve compliance governance and controls. Lead and implement an effective Compliance Program for the regulated entities to ensure it operates in accordance with the licensing obligations.
  • Controls: Assist in the review that Compliance controls are fit for purpose and address the regulatory requirements. Assist in detailing the outputs of the assessments and in working with the business on developing remediation plans to mitigate regulatory risks where required.
  • Education and advocacy: monitor training programmes, both recurring and ad-hoc, to ensure relevant audiences, including new joiners and all relevant stakeholders remain relevant with the firm’s policies and procedures.
  • Assurance and audits: enable effective assurance by supporting internal reviews and external audits of the business as required, including inputting to the risk assessment, plan, execution, and remediation of reviews. Assist the business to devise and close out on corrective action plans. Participate and assist in the identification of policy breaches and in providing appropriate reporting to management.
  • Compliance Monitoring: To support a dynamic compliance environment by assisting in the development and maintenance of a comprehensive compliance monitoring and assurance programme.

title: STS Vendor Master Data Management Final Reviewer Specialist
description:
Job Description

Position Overview



Our company's Global Business Solutions (GBS) organization plays a pivotal role in designing, governing, and executing global processes. Within GBS, the Source to Settle (StS) organization takes charge of ensuring the timely and efficient processing of employee purchase orders, supplier invoices, and payments. The StS process encompasses various critical activities, including Vendor Master Data setup, Supplier Onboarding, Purchasing, Invoicing, Settlements, as well as StS Support.



The Vendor Master Data Final Review Specialist is responsible for overseeing the qualification, analysis, accuracy, and change control of Vendor Master Data. Working independently, this role leverages their expertise in the VMD platform, business processes, and Global Work Instruction to address any issues related to master data. Collaborating with other processes, when necessary, the Specialist ensures effective communication and interaction with Operational and Information Stewards to ensure the data is suitable for its intended purpose and to resolve any master data-related concerns. The Specialist plays a crucial role in qualifying and classifying data, ensuring the precision and completeness of all information. Additionally, they provide valuable recommendations to enhance workflow, increase efficiency, and capitalize on automation opportunities.



Position Responsibilities

Primary responsibilities for this position include, but are not limited to, the following:

Perform the final review of received data creations and changes to companies master data records by ensuring accuracy, completion and adherence to procedure.

Support and execute creations and Changes for non 3rd party vendor account types to support.

Ensure master data integrity in key systems and maintain the processes to support the data quality.

Develop and maintain a comprehensive understanding of all Vendor Master Data and process-related policies and procedures to effectively interface with internal and external clients and to proactively comply with audit requirements.

Execute Vendor Master Data periodical data audits to ensure data is in compliance with Global Work Instructions.

Review and analyze system and data governance reports to ensure high-quality data.

Support departmental reports and metrics generation.

Monitor data, analyze reports and track specific activity to ensure records are synchronized. Acts to resolve all issues and discrepancies.

Support other team members by providing cover when required.

Provide Operation support (Training, Confirmations etc.)

Ensure compliance with data privacy.

Support or deliver other activities and special projects as directed by the workstream MDM Domain Lead or MDM Sr. Specialist

Identify areas for data quality improvements, resolve data quality problems by providing support through the appropriate choice of error detection and data cleansing and correction, process control and improvement, or process design strategies collaborating with subject matter experts (SMEs) and data stewards to meet customer requirements while adhering to published data standards.

Provide transactional support to employees working in the StS space or using StS services, including in the regional Business Service Centers (BSC)

Resolve global transactional issues and deviations as needed and address process performance Anomalies.

Assure root cause analysis of errors and non-compliant items are being performed and corrective actions are being implemented.

Ensure all GBS Global Documentation is aligned to the process structure and design, is up to date, complete and relevant, including SOX controls.

Collaborate with other Process Stewards (Procure to Pay/Settlement, Accounting to Reporting, Customer Master Data…) in all our Company divisions to ensure continuity and alignment across global end-to-end processes.

Support Company merger and divestitures efforts as needed from a Vendor Master Data existing supplier review.

Perform mass data uploads required and ensure the accuracy and compliance of large data sets.

Compliance, Communication & Training

Involved in the development and documentation of processes with other functional data owners.

Support the development of StS content to ensure accurate communication and standard training.

Help educate and support our Company employees on the StS process and tools.

Maintain files and documentation thoroughly and accurately in accordance with company policy and accepted accounting practices.

Ensure compliance with company policies and procedures and supports company mission, values and standards of ethics and integrity.

Support the rollout and enhancements of Master Data Platforms.

Work closely with the STS/business /IT to ensure alignment of master data rules and the operations of the application meet all requirements.





Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in business, Accounting or Finance or related fields preferred

Minimum of two (2) years' relevant work experience.

Knowledge of VMD platforms required.

Broad understanding and knowledge of applicable business processes including end-to-end process use of data and lifecycle of data (creation to use to inactivation).

Fluency oral and written communication in English required

Teamwork and collaborative focus, customer service oriented.

Ability to function in a high-volume setting with tight deadlines.

Attention to details and accuracy focus.

Good analytical and problem-solving skills.

Knowledge of SAP required



Preferred Skills

Ability to work independently and with a team in a fast-paced and high-volume environment with emphasis on accuracy and timeliness.

Good communication skills and ability to manage stakeholders’ requests in an efficient and assertive manner with global stakeholders.

Positive, engaging disposition with high personal integrity, credibility, and energy.

Business level of Spanish / Portuguese / Japanese / Arabic TBC/ language (both written and spoken) Preferred.

Strong communication and interpersonal skills that are effective with various cultures.

SAP Experience preferred.

Intermediate to Advanced PC skills (MS Excel, Word, PowerPoint) .

Ability to operate independently and remain focused through change or uncertainty.

Possess a high degree of integrity and personal ethics in implementing corporate policies and procedures.

Strong customer service and collaboration mind-set

Willingness to attend or conduct remote meetings during off hours (less than 5% of the time)



Physical Position Requirements

Location of role : Malaysia

Account Collections, Adaptability, Analytical Problem Solving, Balance Sheet Account Reconciliations, Business Support, Compliance SOX, Credit Management, Financial Accounting Controls, Financial Operations, Human Resources (HR) Shared Services Advisory, Interpersonal Relationships, Preparation of Financial Reports, Project Management, Quantitative Analytics, Vendor Management

title: Counselor I
description:

Statement of Purpose

Under the direct supervision of the Program Director/Supervisor, the Counselor I provides treatment and recovery services to participating clients, monitors, documents, and supports client treatment progress, maintains ethical and evidence-based care, and participates in treatment team activities.

Major Tasks, Duties and Responsibilities

  • Conduct comprehensive substance use screening, care planning, and treatment activities.

  • Develop individualized care plans in collaboration with clients and treatment team.

  • Provide evidence-based services (e.g., CBT, MI, DBT, Seeking Safety) to assigned group and/or individual caseload.

  • Support clients with relapse prevention, life and coping skills, discharge and aftercare planning, and recovery support.

  • Develop general knowledge of evidence-based practices, medications for addiction treatment, co-occurring disorders, community resources, self-help support, and treatment philosophies.

  • Coordinate with medical providers, social services, and other community resources.

  • Monitor client progress and maintain accurate and timely treatment records and progress notes (e.g., daily activities, service entries, intake and discharge documentation, etc.).

  • Perform toxicology testing, take and record vitals as needed; chart relevant information.

  • For Counselors assigned to residential programs, make rounds every 30 minutes for 72 hours on withdrawal management clients, document and record withdrawal symptoms.

  • For Counselors assigned to residential programs, observe and document client self- administration of medications.

  • Ensure compliance with regulatory and accreditation standards, including but not limited to DMH, DHCS, SAPC, HIPAA, 42 CFR Part 2, CARF, etc.

  • Assist clients with benefits, housing, vocational, and community reintegration needs.

  • Respond to behavioral crises, medical emergencies, suicidal ideation, overdose including administration of anti-overdose medications as needed, or acute intoxication safely, within scope of practice.

  • Occasionally provide transportation for clients including DPSS and other linkages.

  • Report and record any changes observed in client condition or behavior, including unusual incidents. Identify, report, and assist with the management of emergencies.

  • Participate in safety programming to promote client and staff safety. Maintain health and safety standards of facility.

  • Attend supervision, clinical meetings, and continuing education to maintain credentials.

  • Participate in treatment team meetings, case conferences, and program planning.

  • Contribute to agency quality assurance and improvement initiatives.

  • Maintain professional boundaries and standards. Treat clients with respect, care, and concern. Comply with confidentiality requirements at all times.

  • Maintain familiarity with BHS policies and procedures and other applicable regulations; perform job duties accordingly. Represent BHS well in all contacts.

  • Courteously answer phones, appropriately directing calls and taking messages. Facilitate client external communication as approved by supervisor.

  • Attend meetings and trainings and participate in committees as assigned.

  • Other duties as assigned.

Counselor I Competencies and Performance Expectations:

  • Ability to complete the above major tasks, duties, and responsibilities.

  • Ability to demonstrate professional judgment and decision-making, including the ability to recognize and seek out supervision and/or consultation when required.

  • Ability to demonstrate familiarity with and practice of 12 core competencies for SUD counselors.

  • Ability to effectively document in required note structures (e.g., SOAP, GIRP, etc.).

  • Ability to recognize the symptoms and develop knowledge of appropriate treatment associated with substance use and co-occurring disorders (i.e., mental health, medical health, etc.).

  • Ability to identify and respond appropriately to a crisis within scope of practice including but not limited to overdose, behavioral challenges, contraband protocol, emergency codes, etc.

  • Ability to screen and/or assess for acute intoxication and withdrawal symptoms within scope of practice.

  • Ability to meet productivity standards as assigned.

  • Ability to recognize personal biases within diverse populations. Maintain cultural sensitivity at all times.

  • Ability to adhere to professional standards.

title: Maintenance Planner/Scheduler
description:
If you are currently employed at Smithfield, please log into Workday and submit your application through the Jobs Hub.If you are currently employed at Smithfield, please log into Workday and submit your application through the Jobs Hub.

Have a seat at our table. When you join Smithfield, you become part of something special – a company that's sustainably feeding people around the world, producing good food the right way with respect for our people, animals, communities and planet. With opportunities across locations and functions, a culture grounded in our Core Four values - gratitude, communication, respect and accountability - and a strong commitment to learning, collaboration, and innovation, Smithfield offers challenging and rewarding careers where you can grow, contribute and make a real impact. Apply Now!

THE VALUE YOU'LL BRING:

This dynamic dual-role position is at the heart of ensuring seamless operations by overseeing and driving the entire maintenance work control process. You’ll be the mastermind behind prioritizing maintenance work, developing detailed job plans, and determining the right parts, materials, crafts, and skills needed to get the job done. By assigning work control plans to supervisors, you will ensure the efficient execution of maintenance tasks by our skilled hourly staff. You'll also provide essential equipment expertise and technical guidance to continuously enhance maintenance activities, while occasionally stepping into a leadership role to manage both Smithfield employees and contractors.

As the owner and manager of the Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) at the plant level, you will be the go-to expert ensuring that all systems run smoothly and efficiently. In this role, you'll support safety programs as required. If you're ready to lead, innovate, and make an impact, this is your opportunity!

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

The below statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this job. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of personnel so classified. May perform other duties as assigned.

  • Maintenance Planning & Execution: You'll plan maintenance while ensuring compliance with regulations (e.g., OSHA, EPA, USDA). You'll also develop and maintain maintenance procedures, prioritize work orders, and ensure materials/tools are available. Review and update completed work orders and machinery history in the CMMS system. Generate reports on work progress, schedules, and personnel vacation. Produce weekly maintenance schedules and forecast workforce needs. Manage MRO inventory, including stocking, parts disbursements, returns, and audits.

  • Training & Personnel Management: You'll also train maintenance personnel on reporting procedures and using CMMS software. Assist in contractor qualifications and performance management. Train department personnel in PSM program elements.

  • Process Safety Management (PSM) & Compliance: Organize and maintain information for the 14 PSM elements. Develop and manage a process safety information library in line with OSHA 1910.119. Assist with Process Hazard Analyses (PHA), audits, and compliance tracking. Manage the Management of Change (MOC) Program, track submittals, and develop operating procedures. Perform hazard assessments, assist with Pre-Startup Safety Reviews (PSSR), and audit the PSM program. Keep PSM and EPA documentation up to date for compliance.

  • Reporting & Documentation: You will assist with annual program goals, provide reports, and ensure documentation is available for audits. Maintain compliance documentation for PSM and other regulatory requirements.

  • Leadership: Provides leadership and guidance to employees in the Maintenance Department.

WHAT WE'RE SEEKING:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals to perform the essential functions.

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited four-year college or university in Engineering or a related field; or equivalent combination of education and experience, required.

  • Working knowledge of basic computer skills, Internet and Microsoft Office including Word and Excel.

  • Strong problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to work well with others in fast paced, dynamic environment.

  • Ability to be respectful, approachable and team oriented while building strong working relationships and a positive work environment.

OTHER SKILLS THAT MAKE YOU STAND OUT:

  • Experience in the supervision of day-to-day preventive and corrective maintenance, strongly preferred.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

  • Project management software experience is preferred.

  • Knowledge of the CMMS system, preferred.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT:

  • The plant environment will include wet or humid conditions (non-weather related), extreme cold and heat (non-weather related), working near moving mechanical parts, exposure to fumes or airborne particles, and chemicals.

  • Noise level in the work environment is usually moderate but can be loud when in the production area.

  • Frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.

  • Specific vision abilities required include close vision, distance vision and ability to adjust focus.

  • Frequently required to stand; walk; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl and talk or hear.

Yes

title: VP Engineering
description:
VP Engineering

Overview and purpose of the role

The purpose of this role is to:

  • Ensure that products are delivered according to roadmaps, meet design requirements, are manufacturable and consistently achieve positive experiences with customers
  • Management and leadership of the Engineering team
  • Hiring new talent
  • Maintain compliance with quality standards
  • Contribute to the Company’s strategy

Responsibilities

Leadership and management of the Engineering Team

  • Contribute to company strategy and priorities as a member of the executive team.
  • Lead, mentor and develop Engineering, recruiting the talent and building the capabilities needed to deliver business goals.
  • Set clear objectives, responsibilities and delivery commitments, supporting technical specialists to succeed

Product development and manufacturing

  • Own engineering delivery across the product lifecycle, from R&D handover and platform development through qualification, manufacturing introduction and ongoing support.
  • Build realistic programme plans, define work packages and dependencies, allocate resources and manage change, escalating risks and delivery issues early.
  • Work with Sales and Field Applications to translate customer requirements into achievable engineering commitments and support design wins.
  • Ensure products meet performance, quality, reliability and applicable industrial, medical and automotive qualification requirements.
  • Deliver manufacturing test solutions that meet cost, yield and capacity targets.
  • Work with Operations, Quality and manufacturing partners to select suppliers and transfer products from pilot production to volume manufacture.
  • Identify opportunities to improve Flusso’s products and platforms.

Engineering capability

  • Establish proportionate engineering processes, standards and lifecycle practices that improve quality, repeatability and delivery efficiency.
  • Ensure teams have the equipment, software tools and facilities needed to deliver high-quality work.
  • Maintain safe, organised and well-maintained test laboratories, including compliant waste management.
  • Support compliance with ISO 9001 and ISO 14001 requirements and drive continual improvement.

Business support activities

  • Manage engineering budgets and capacity in line with business priorities.
  • Build effective relationships across Engineering, Sales, Field Applications, Operations, Quality and external partners.
  • Support key customer and supplier engagements, business development and marketing activities.
  • Pursue relevant government-funded R&D initiatives and technology partnerships.
  • Communicate engineering priorities, programme progress, risks and resource needs clearly to staff, the executive team and the Board.

Requirements

Qualifications, knowledge, skills and experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant Engineering or Science subject.
  • Demonstrable experience leading engineering teams delivering complex hardware products through development, qualification and manufacturing introduction.
  • Strong programme planning and delivery skills, including resource planning, work-package definition, dependency management, change management, risk control and early escalation.
  • Experience introducing or improving fit-for-purpose engineering processes and product lifecycle practices that improve quality and repeatability without unnecessary bureaucracy.
  • Good technical breadth across relevant hardware product development, such as electronics, firmware, software, mechanical integration, prototyping, semiconductor or MEMS manufacturing. The role leads technical specialists; it is not the company’s principal technical authority.
  • Experience working closely with Sales, Field Applications, Operations, Quality and manufacturing partners in a customer-led business.
  • Knowledge of ISO9001 and ISO14001 quality standards and procedures.

Profile

  • A delivery-focused engineering leader who makes commitments visible, builds realistic plans and helps teams deliver on time and to the required quality.
  • Able to lead and develop technical specialists, challenge and clarify requests constructively, and make sound resource decisions.
  • Customer-aware and commercially grounded, with the judgement to balance delivery speed, quality, risk and engineering capacity.
  • Introduces useful engineering discipline while keeping processes proportionate, practical and suited to a fast-moving business.
  • Collaborative and decisive, with clear communication across Engineering, Field Apps, Sales, Operations, Quality, the executive team and external partners.
  • Pro active by nature, comfortable working in a technology-led, evolving business and willing to travel as required, including to partners in Europe and Asia.

Benefits

  • Base salary
  • Bonus (% of base salary) based on company and personal performance
  • Workplace pension contribution 3% of full base salary (we can trade with salary level for higher)
  • Bupa Cash Plan Level 3 (employee only)
  • Private Medical insurance with cover for spouse/partner and dependent children
  • Group Life Insurance covers up to 4 x salary
  • 25 days holiday plus bank holidays (adjusted for part time roles)
  • Support for relocation (loan discharged over two years service)
  • Hybrid home/office working, by agreement with line manager

title: Staff Software Engineer
description:
Procore Technologies is the leading technology partner for every stage of construction. We empower construction teams to drive efficiency and mitigate risk through actionable AI & data-driven insights. For over 20 years, we have been transforming the industry with purpose-built solutions for construction professionals and we’re looking for talented people to help us build together.


We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer, Full Stack to help drive the technical direction of our projects and develop products that impact how communities' hospitals, homes, sports stadiums, and schools across the world are built. As the Staff Software Engineer, Full Stack on our Portfolio Management team, you will work closely with Engineering, Product, and UX teams to design and build scalable solutions that delight users and solve critical business problems. Your strengths in full-stack architecture, distributed systems design, and technical mentorship will drive your success.


You will report to the Senior Manager, Software Engineering and will be based in our Bengaluru, India office.


What You’ll Do

  • Evolve our existing codebase from a monolithic Rails application into a modular system with clear, well-enforced domain boundaries and a coherent public interface
  • Contribute to designing and building a scalable architecture that aligns with our long-term technical vision
  • Work across the stack to ship robust code for our Rails backend and React frontend, leveraging PostgreSQL for complex querying needs
  • Enhance performance, flexibility, scalability, and security across backend services and database layers
  • Collaborate with TypeScript and React to create intuitive, consistent, and accessible user experiences on the front end
  • Partner cross-functionally with Engineering, Product, and UX to define and deliver solutions that solve critical business problems
  • Communicate complex technical problems, trade-offs, and architectural solutions to both technical and non-technical stakeholders through clear documentation
  • Collaborate across engineering teams on large-scale platform initiatives to advance our goal of connecting construction stakeholders worldwide

What You Bring

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, a related technical field, or comparable practical work experience
  • Demonstrated extensive full-stack development experience, preferably with Ruby on Rails on the backend, and React or Angular on the frontend
  • Strong foundation in Object-Oriented Programming, Test-Driven Development, Service-Oriented Architecture, and software design principles
  • Comprehensive knowledge of end-to-end web development lifecycles, including testing, staging, deployment, monitoring, and observability
  • Proven experience collaborating effectively within an Agile/Scrum engineering environment
  • Demonstrated expertise in building, documenting, and maintaining robust APIs using REST or GraphQL
  • Proven track record of anticipating technical bottlenecks in complex projects and architecting effective solutions
  • Professional English communication proficiency (both spoken and written)

Strong-fit Background Might Include

  • Staff Software Engineer / Lead Full Stack Engineer
  • Principal Software Engineer / Senior Full Stack Architect
  • Backend Systems Architect (Ruby on Rails / Distributed Microservices)
  • Frontend Platform Lead (Modern React / TypeScript Ecosystem)

title: Library Operations Supervisor, Penn State Lehigh Valley
description:
APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS:

  • CURRENT PENN STATE EMPLOYEE (faculty, staff, technical service, or student), please login to Workday to complete the internal application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday.

  • CURRENT PENN STATE STUDENT (not employed previously at the university) and seeking employment with Penn State, please login to Workday to complete the student application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday.

  • If you are NOT a current employee or student, please click “Apply” and complete the application process for external applicants.

Approval of remote and hybrid work is not guaranteed regardless of work location. For additional information on remote work at Penn State, see Notice to Out of State Applicants.

​

POSITION SPECIFICS​

Penn State Lehigh Valley Library is seeking a Library Operations Supervisor to lead the daily operations of its library with an emphasis on circulation, collection maintenance, and customer service.


This position offers an excellent opportunity to provide front-facing customer service within a prestigious library system, while overseeing and supporting library staff and student assistants.


You will get to partner with many others at Penn State Lehigh Valley and across the Pennsylvania State University Libraries as you support our students, faculty, and campus – giving you the opportunity to learn from and/or offer guidance to fellow employees.


Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Facilitate and lead the daily operations of the library including coordination of circulation, reserves, interlibrary loan, acquisitions, catalog maintenance, and collection maintenance
  • Supervise library staff (i.e., hire, schedule, train, and conduct performance management) including a few full-time and part-time staff and several student employees
  • Provide outstanding customer service to students, faculty, and community users (e.g., answering questions; resolving concerns; instructing patrons in technology, systems, and equipment; and administering policies for library users)
  • Develop and implement operational procedures
  • Collaborate with the Head Librarian on planning, implementing, and evaluating unit priorities including analysis and improvement of library services and assisting with projects and initiatives that advance library priorities
  • Monitor budgets including ordering and reconciling supplies purchases, forecasting and budget planning
  • Maintain records, compile and analyze data, prepare reports, develop and maintain process documentation
  • Represent the library and the campus by serving as the primary contact with selected Penn State units and through service on committees
  • May engage in other initiatives and projects depending on the skills and interests of the successful candidate and the needs of the department

Joining a small yet impactful and supportive team, the Library Operations Supervisor will work independently and collaboratively to complete the above responsibilities.


Library staff are also cross trained to complete duties in multiple areas as needed.


To perform the essential functions of this position, the Library Operations Supervisor will regularly move around the library and physically manage collections and equipment (e.g., carrying, shifting, and shelving books; pushing book carts; handling laptops), with or without reasonable accommodation.


Work Location & Schedule:

The Penn State Lehigh Valley Library’s current hours of operation during the academic year are from 8 a.m. to 7 p.m. Eastern from Monday through Thursday and 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Eastern on Friday.


The Library Operations Supervisor will be expected to regularly work shifts which provide consistent afternoon and evening coverage. Work schedules will be established in consultation with the Head Librarian and may vary to meet operational needs (e.g., during the summer and student breaks).


Infrequent weekend work may be required to support library events.


Important Note: This position requires regular on-site work.


Qualifications:

Required Qualifications:

  • Committed to providing excellent customer service; demonstrated ability to be adaptable, flexible, and patient with customers and staff
  • Excellent interpersonal skills; inclusive and respectful when working with others
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills
  • Ability to stay organized with a high attention to detail and accuracy while multi-tasking
  • Experience providing leadership or guidance to others, demonstrated through formal supervisory responsibilities or by serving as an informal team lead or go‑to resource for questions and problem-solving
  • Ability and willingness to learn job-related software
  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365 tools or comparable software used for communication, documentation, and spreadsheet management

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience working in a library setting, utilizing library systems (strongly preferred)
  • Experience working with circulating technologies
  • Experience managing departmental budgets

MINIMUM EDUCATION, WORK EXPERIENCE & REQUIRED CERTIFICATIONS

If filled as Library Operations Supervisor - Senior Supervisor, this position requires:
Bachelor's Degree
6+ years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience accepted
Required Certifications:
None

If filled as Library Operations Supervisor - Supervisor, this position requires:
Bachelor's Degree
3+ years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience accepted
Required Certifications:
None

Important Application Instructions:

Applicants must submit a cover letter addressing their interest and relevant experience, in addition to a resume.


Additional Information:

The Pennsylvania State University Libraries is supportive of flexible work arrangements when aligned with the ability to meet the needs of the unit and the essential duties of the position. Questions related to flexible work should be directed to the hiring manager during the interview process.


This position will report to the Head Librarian of the Penn State Lehigh Valley Library.


The Penn State Lehigh Valley Library provides the Penn State Lehigh Valley campus community with access to all resources and services offered by the Penn State University Libraries – one of the Top 10 research libraries in North America.


Penn State Lehigh Valley is located in Center Valley, Pennsylvania. The Allentown–Bethlehem–Easton metropolitan area, which includes the Lehigh Valley, is Pennsylvania's third-most populous metropolitan area after Philadelphia and Pittsburgh.


The Lehigh Valley is a historically rich and economically vibrant area.

BACKGROUND CHECKS/CLEARANCES

Employment with the University will require successful completion of background check(s) in accordance with University policies.

Penn State does not sponsor or take over sponsorship of a staff employment Visa. Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S.

SALARY & BENEFITS

The salary range for this position, including all possible grades, is $44,628.00 - $71,340.00.

Salary Structure - Information on Penn State's salary structure

Penn State provides a competitive benefits package for full-time employees designed to support both personal and professional well-being. In addition to comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, employees enjoy robust retirement plans and substantial paid time off which includes holidays, vacation and sick time. One of the standout benefits is the generous 75% tuition discount, available to employees as well as eligible spouses and children. For more detailed information, please visit our Benefits Page.

CAMPUS SECURITY CRIME STATISTICS

Pursuant to the Jeanne Clery Disclosure of Campus Security Policy and Campus Crime Statistics Act and the Pennsylvania Act of 1988, Penn State publishes a combined Annual Security and Annual Fire Safety Report (ASR). The ASR includes crime statistics and institutional policies concerning campus security, such as those concerning alcohol and drug use, crime prevention, the reporting of crimes, sexual assault, and other matters. The ASR is available for review here.

EEO IS THE LAW

Penn State is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to providing employment opportunities to all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. If you are unable to use our online application process due to an impairment or disability, please contact 814-865-1473.

Penn State is committed to and accountable for advancing equity, respect, and belonging. We embrace individual uniqueness, as well as a culture of belonging that supports equity initiatives, leverages the educational and institutional benefits of inclusion in society, and provides opportunities for engagement intended to help all members of the community thrive. We value belonging as a core strength and an essential element of the university’s teaching, research, and service mission.

title: Software Engineer (C#/.NET, Azure)
description:
WHY THIS ROLE IS IMPORTANT TO US

SimCorp is developing a new game changing Software-as-a-Service solution for Performance Measurement and Attribution, which will allow Investment Managers to interact with, and analyze their investments in a modern web application. It is connected to a high-performance computing calculation engine in the back-end, thus combining more than 50 years of industry-leading experience of SimCorp with a modern user experience and cloud computing, enabling users to do in minutes what used to take hours.

We welcome applications from both early‑career and mid‑career software engineers.

WHAT YOU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

  • Build solutions: collaborate closely with your team, Product Managers, Architects, peers and end-users to deliver high-quality, secure and valuable solutions in the Performance Product Area.
  • Contribute across the entire development lifecycle - from requirements analysis and design to implementation, test automation, documentation, and ongoing support.
  • Coordinate and execute on development and maintenance of the investment performance solution in collaboration with product owners and other teams.
  • Think beyond the code: Understand our strategy, goals and customer needs to enhance SimCorp’s impact.
  • You will work closely with experienced engineers who support your development. Over time, you will grow into taking ownership of larger components and may mentor more junior colleagues as your experience grows.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

  • Solid knowledge of C#, .NET Core/Framework, and object-oriented design principles.
  • Experience with APIs.
  • Familiarity with modern engineering practices, including CI/CD pipelines and trunk-based development. We use Git (Azure DevOps).
  • Interest in cloud engineering. We use Microsoft Azure.
  • You understand the importance of automated testing of business‑critical functionality and quality assurance practices.
  • Willingness to dive into a complex domain, working with finance, investment performance & attribution and investment-related instruments.
  • You are able to solve complex problems in a structured manner.
  • You are enthusiastic about building state-of-the-art software, and have the mindset needed to make others understand your ideas.
  • Curiosity and adaptability to learn in-house tools and frameworks - including the APL programming language (no prior experience in APL required, we provide extensive training).
  • You are good at coordinating with both programmers and non-programmers, to ensure a full understanding of tasks.
  • You have a Master’s degree or higher within Computer Sciences, Engineering, Finance, Physics, Mathematics, Economics or similar experience.
  • If you have knowledge of a financial domain it is plus, otherwise we will bring you up to speed using technical discussions, training and a comprehensive onboarding program.

WHAT IS IT LIKE TO WORK HERE

SimCorp plans work in an agile manner, using 4 planning intervals (PI’s) per year, each consisting of 5 sprints of 2 weeks each, followed by a 3-week Innovation and Planning sprint, which can be used for mastering skills in various areas, or more freely investigating ideas with prototypes. It is important that our people learn and grow constantly, and SimCorp invests a lot to foster the continuous learning environment to support people on their journeys.

BENEFITS

Competitive salary, bonus scheme, and pension are essential for any work agreement. However, in SimCorp, we believe we can offer more. Therefore, in addition to the traditional benefit scheme, we provide an excellent work & life balance: flexible work hours, a hybrid workplace model. On top of that, we have IP sprints where you have 3 weeks per quarter you can spend on mastering your skills as well as contributing to the company development. There is never just only one route - we practice an individual approach to professional development to support the direction you want to take.

WHO WE ARE?

For over 50 years, we have worked closely with investment and asset managers to become the world’s leading provider of integrated investment management solutions. We are 3,000+ colleagues with a broad range of nationalities, educations, professional experiences, ages, and backgrounds.

SimCorp is an independent subsidiary of the Deutsche Börse Group. Following the recent merger with Axioma, we leverage the combined strength of our brands to provide an industry-leading, full, front-to-back offering for our clients.

SimCorp is an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, without regard to race, gender, age, disability, or any other protected status under applicable law. We are committed to building a culture where diverse perspectives and expertise are integrated into our everyday work. We believe in the continual growth and development of our employees, so that we can provide best-in-class solutions to our clients.
