title: Global Marketing & Digital Wealth Delivery Manager(Fixed-term)
location: BU3-Budapest-GTC White House, Vaci ut 47, District XIII, Budapest
description:
About this role

The Team:

The Global Marketing & Digital Wealth organization at BlackRock is a forward-looking, globally connected team at the center of the firm’s most high-impact priorities. We are architects of growth, working across functions and markets to unlock opportunities and accelerate outcomes for the business. In collaboration with both internal and external partners, we design the conditions for success—delivering next-generation campaigns, brand platforms, communications, training, and client experiences. Our work is powered by world-class centers of excellence spanning content strategy, research & analytics, and digital platforms & experiences.


Within Global Marketing & Digital Wealth, the Global Digital team owns and transforms BlackRock’s client-facing digital properties—including BlackRock.com, iShares.com, and Advisor Center—as well as our email marketing channels. The team brings together product, design, engineering, and digital expertise to create connected, personalized experiences that help clients discover, understand, and engage with BlackRock.


Role and Impact:

We believe the future of ETF distribution is digital. As ETF adoption accelerates around the world, we have a unique opportunity to shape the future of the investment industry. We are on a mission to transform iShares.com, to inspire and champion investor progress by creating the most trusted, valued, and relevant digital experience.


We’re looking for a Delivery Manager (maternity cover) to join our Digital Experiences team to support the development and build of the iShares.com websites. The successful candidate will adapt quickly to new circumstances as they arise, working within a multi-disciplined development team to guide growth, refine processes, and enable the team to build and run outstanding products using agile methodologies. This role reports directly to the Delivery Lead, based in Budapest. The Budapest office is our primary work location, and all employees must work from the office at least four days per week.


Responsibilities:

  • Work within a multi-disciplined development team supporting the team, guiding growth, and refining processes, enabling the team to build and run outstanding product using agile methodologies.
  • Remove impediments and blockers on a day-to-day basis.
  • Work with the Product Manager and team to define the roadmap of the product delivery.
  • Lead the collaborative planning process for each sprint, helping the team to prioritise and self-organise around the work, keeping in mind their capability and capacity.
  • Facilitate the team’s meetings (Planning, Daily Stand-Up, Refinement, Retrospective, etc.) as well as other workshops as needed by the team and business.
  • Guide, mentor, and coach team members and partners on agile and scrum principles and practices.
  • Be responsible for the development process, guiding the team through continuous improvements and release cycles.
  • Coordinate the release preparation and release process.
  • Create, collate, and understand progress metrics with the team.
  • Engage with the Delivery Management community, sharing practices, developing each other, and experimenting in a safe space.

Core Skills:

  • Excellent people and communication skills.
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills.
  • A calm, dedicated, and optimistic individual.
  • Ability to work independently.
  • Coaching-oriented—develops teams and partners in agile ways of working.

Qualifications:

  • 1–3 years as a Scrum Master working with software development teams delivering complex projects.
  • Experienced in project management and/or facilitation, coaching, and mentoring.
  • Extensive use of JIRA, Confluence, Azure, Miro, Conceptboard, or other online collaboration and management tools.


The salary range for Hungary is 13400000 - 20100000 HUF

Additionally, employees are eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, and benefits including healthcare, leave benefits, and retirement benefits. BlackRock operates a pay-for-performance compensation philosophy and your total compensation may vary based on role, location, and firm, department and individual performance.

Our benefits

To help you stay energized, engaged and inspired, we offer a wide range of employee benefits including: retirement investment and tools designed to help you in building a sound financial future; access to education reimbursement; comprehensive resources to support your physical health and emotional well-being; family support programs; and Flexible Time Off (FTO) so you can relax, recharge and be there for the people you care about.

Our hybrid work model

BlackRock’s hybrid work model is designed to enable a culture of collaboration and apprenticeship that enriches the experience of our employees, while supporting flexibility for all. Employees are currently required to work at least 4 days in the office per week, with the flexibility to work from home 1 day a week. Some business groups may require more time in the office due to their roles and responsibilities. We remain focused on increasing the impactful moments that arise when we work together in person – aligned with our commitment to performance and innovation. As a new joiner, you can count on this hybrid model to accelerate your learning and onboarding experience here at BlackRock.


Guidance on AI use for candidates


At BlackRock, AI has long been part of how we work – enhancing decision-making, improving operations, and helping us deliver better outcomes for clients. We encourage candidates to use AI thoughtfully to learn, prepare, and work more effectively; but during our interview process, we want to focus on getting to know you through your own experiences, thinking, and judgment. To support you, we’ve provided guidance on when and how to use AI during our hiring process so you can approach each step with confidence and showcase your best self.


About BlackRock


At BlackRock, we are all connected by one mission: to help more and more people experience financial well-being. Our clients, and the people they serve, are saving for retirement, paying for their children’s educations, buying homes and starting businesses. Their investments also help to strengthen the global economy: support businesses small and large; finance infrastructure projects that connect and power cities; and facilitate innovations that drive progress.


This mission would not be possible without our smartest investment – the one we make in our employees. It’s why we’re dedicated to creating an environment where our colleagues feel welcomed, valued and supported with networks, benefits and development opportunities to help them thrive.


To learn more about BlackRock, please visit Careers.BlackRock.com. We also encourage you to get to know us on LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube, X, and TikTok.


BlackRock is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to age, disability, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation and other protected characteristics at law.

title: Operational Coach Media Productie
description:
Job Description

Krijg jij energie van mensen laten groeien, samen resultaten neerzetten en iedere dag de operatie beter maken? Dan is dit misschien jouw volgende stap.

Voor onze afdeling zijn wij op zoek naar een Operational Coach Media Productie.

Welkom in ons team

Binnen Media Productie maken we hoogwaardige kweekmedia, buffers en agarplaten die essentieel zijn voor productie, R&D en laboratoria. Met circa 1.500 verschillende producten en 2.500 batches per jaar is onze omgeving veelzijdig, uitdagend en volop in beweging.

We werken in een GMP-omgeving waarin People, Safety, Quality, Delivery en Cost iedere dag samenkomen. Juist daar kun jij als Operational Coach het verschil maken.

Over de rol

Als Operational Coach geef je leiding aan onze Operators en Senior Operators. Je staat dicht bij je team en de operatie, weet wat er speelt en zorgt voor heldere prioriteiten en duidelijke verwachtingen. Tegelijk geef je medewerkers het vertrouwen en de ruimte om zelf verantwoordelijkheid te nemen.

Wat ga je doen?

  • Coachen en ontwikkelen: je helpt medewerkers groeien in vakmanschap, eigenaarschap en samenwerking.
  • Richting geven: je brengt focus aan en stuurt op veiligheid, kwaliteit, planning, output en kosten.
  • Samen resultaten behalen: je bouwt met de Senior Operator(s) aan een sterke en zelfstandige dagelijkse operatie.
  • Continu verbeteren: je stimuleert het team om problemen niet alleen op te lossen, maar processen structureel beter te maken.
  • Verbinden: je werkt nauw samen met onder andere QA, M&R, Engineering, EHS en Planning.
  • Je hoeft niet alles zelf te weten of op te lossen. De Production Expert is jouw functionele rechterhand voor complexe proces-, systeem-, equipment- en compliancevraagstukken. Jij focust op mensen, richting en performance. De Production Expert voegt inhoudelijke diepgang toe. Samen bouwen jullie aan een sterke en toekomstgerichte operatie.

Jouw profiel

We zoeken een Leader die zichtbaar en benaderbaar is, goed luistert, duidelijke keuzes durft te maken en mensen in hun kracht zet.

  • HBO werk- en denkniveau;
  • Ervaring met het aansturen, coachen en ontwikkelen van medewerkers, waaronder het effectief leidinggeven aan een team van minimaal 5 medewerkers;
  • Ervaring binnen een productieomgeving, bij voorkeur binnen GMP;
  • Sterke communicatieve en coachende vaardigheden;
  • Een praktische, positieve en resultaatgerichte instelling;
  • Het vermogen om overzicht te houden en prioriteiten te stellen;
  • Affiniteit met Lean, SPS en Continuous Improvement.

Wat we bieden

Werken bij onze organisatie betekent samen werken aan gezondheid in een internationale werkomgeving met toegewijde collega’s. Je krijgt alle ruimte om jezelf te ontwikkelen en te laten zien wie jij bent. Verder kan je rekenen op aantrekkelijke arbeidsvoorwaarden, zoals:

  • Een competitief salaris.
  • Flexibele dagdienst met werktijden tussen 07:00 en 17:00 uur (een volledige werkdag bedraagt 8 uur).
  • 35,5 vakantiedagen.
  • 8% vakantietoeslag en 3% eindejaarsuitkering.
  • Bonusregeling.
  • Een uitstekend pensioen.
  • Verschillende trainingsmodules en doorgroeimogelijkheden. Operator(s), de Production Expert en specialistische disciplines.

Klaar om samen het verschil te maken?

Als Operational Coach krijg je de kans om écht iets neer te zetten. Niet door alles zelf te doen, maar door mensen te laten groeien, eigenaarschap te stimuleren en samen steeds beter te worden.

Samen met jouw Operators, Senior Operator(s) en Production Expert bouw je aan een Media Productie waarin mensen met plezier en vertrouwen samenwerken en waarin veiligheid, kwaliteit en performance hand in hand gaan.

Jij brengt mensen in beweging.

Job Description:

Endpoint Security Engineer


Advance your career while impacting our national security in cyber as an Endpoint Security Manager at GDIT. Here, technologists have many paths to grow a meaningful career supporting cyber missions and operations across the federal government.


MEANINGFUL WORK AND PERSONAL IMPACT


As an Endpoint Security Engineer, the work you’ll do at GDIT will be impactful to the mission of NATO SOFCOM. You will play a crucial role in maintaining endpoint security tools, policy controls, and detection capabilities for NATO SOFCOM.


  • Administer and optimize Trellix ePolicy Orchestrator (ePO), Endpoint Security (ENS), HX endpoint detection and response and supporting infrastructure.
  • Tune threat and exploit prevention, on-access/on-demand scanning, exclusions, agent deployment, signature updates and endpoint performance.

The Make-Ready Technician is responsible for preparing vacant apartment homes for new residents by completing maintenance, repairs, and cosmetic improvements to company standards. This role plays a critical part in ensuring apartments are move-in ready on schedule and that every resident’s first impression of their home is a positive one.

The Make-Ready Technician works closely with the Maintenance and Property Management teams and may assist with general maintenance needs across the property as required.

title: Planning Officer
description:
Business Overview:

At Sony UK Technology Centre (UK TEC) we have over 500 highly skilled Team Players, who help create some of the most advanced technology on the global market. Alongside producing the latest in broadcast technology, our world-class engineers work on multiple third-party manufacturing products. This collaborative approach to contract manufacturing has produced many commercial successes over the years, including the best-selling British computer of all time, the Raspberry Pi. We also work to pioneer the latest ground-breaking manufacturing processes of the future through the Advanced Manufacturing Research Operations Centre.

What you will be doing:

We are seeking a dynamic and detail-oriented Planning Officer to join our team at Sony UK TEC. As a Planning Officer, you will play a pivotal role in coordinating and optimising our production processes to meet the demands of our customers. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in production planning within the electronics manufacturing sector and possess excellent organisational and communication skills.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop and implement production plans to meet customer demand while optimising resource utilisation and coordinating with Operations, Supply Chain and Procurement teams, including urgent delivery requests.
  • Manage customer sales orders, forecasts and changing requirements in collaboration with Account Managers and external customers.
  • Monitor production capacity, identify bottlenecks and implement adjustments to ensure efficient resource allocation and meet changing customer demands.
  • Manage finished goods inventory against budgets and forecasts, maintaining accurate records, minimising excess stock and ensuring On-Time-In-Full (OTIF) delivery.
  • Own PSI Forecasting & Reporting for a particular business area, preparing and presentation Production, Shipping and Inventory (PSI) forecasts at weekly and monthly business review meetings.
  • Communicate production schedules, delivery timelines, customer requirements and potential delays to relevant internal and external stakeholders.
  • Identify and implement process improvements, best practices and system enhancements to improve planning efficiency and effectiveness.

Essential Criteria:

  • Competent using MS Office - Outlook, PowerPoint, Word, Excel
  • Ability to communicate with and present to all levels of the business.
  • Highly organised with a strong attention to detail
  • Self-motivated with a strong sense of responsibility to deliver to schedules
  • Analytical skills with the ability to identify trends, and make decisions based on the data and options available.
  • Previous experience in capacity planning.

Desirable

  • Experience within a fast-paced manufacturing environment or similar role
  • Knowledge and experience of working with Oracle Database

title: Recovery Worker
description:
Location: 128 Botcherby Avenue, Carlisle, Cumbria, CA1 2TX.

Working Hours: 22.5 hours per week (3 days)

Contract Type: Permanent

Salary: £25,877.80–£34,240 per annum (pro rata)

Please note: The salary listed reflects the full earning potential for this role. Starting salaries depend on experience and progression within the band.

About Waythrough

Waythrough was formed in 2024 following the merger of Humankind and Richmond Fellowship. Together, we’ve created one of the largest mental health and social support charities in England.

Every year, we support around 125,000 people through nearly 200 services – and it’s all made possible by our 3,500 brilliant staff and volunteers.

Make a real difference in your community

Are you passionate about helping others live safer, healthier, more independent lives? Join our team at Waythrough and support people facing challenges around mental health, substance use, housing or domestic abuse. This is more than just a job – it’s a chance to build meaningful relationships and create lasting change.

About the role:


We have an exciting opportunity to join our team as a Recovery Worker, based in Carlisle.


This is a rewarding and varied role where you'll support people to improve their quality of life, develop practical and emotional life skills and work towards greater independence.


You'll provide person-centred, recovery-focused support, helping individuals identify their aspirations, develop meaningful goals and build the confidence and skills they need to achieve positive outcomes.


You'll work closely with people using our services, empowering them to make informed choices, take control of their lives and develop the skills they need to live as independently as possible.


Working as part of a supportive team, you'll contribute to the safe and effective running of the service, promoting choice, inclusion and positive well-being.

This is a part-time, permanent position working 22.5 hours per week over three days. The role will involve occasional evening, night and weekend working when required to meet the needs of the service and the people we support.


In this role, you will:


  • Provide person-centred support, helping individuals improve their physical, mental and emotional well-being.
  • Support people to develop independent living skills, including budgeting, community engagement and accessing appropriate services.
  • Encourage choice, control and active participation, ensuring individuals are at the centre of decisions about their support.
  • Manage an allocated caseload of key clients, developing meaningful and achievable person-centred support plans.
  • Work with individuals to identify their aspirations, set goals and achieve positive outcomes.
  • Promote independence, confidence and social inclusion, supporting people to access community resources and additional services where appropriate.
  • Monitor the well-being and welfare of individuals, identifying concerns and responding appropriately.
  • Develop and implement positive risk assessments in line with organisational policies and procedures.
  • Maintain professional boundaries and ensure all support is delivered in accordance with relevant codes of conduct, safeguarding requirements and organisational policies.
  • Maintain accurate, timely and confidential records using the organisation's electronic database.
  • Work collaboratively with external agencies, community mental health teams, multidisciplinary professionals and carers to ensure coordinated support.
  • Contribute positively to team meetings, handovers and the day-to-day delivery of the service.
  • Manage your own workload effectively, prioritising responsibilities and maintaining your own well-being through appropriate support and supervision.

About you:


You are passionate about helping people make positive changes in their lives and understand the importance of delivering compassionate, inclusive and person-centred support.


You'll have excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build positive relationships, listen to others and respond sensitively to complex situations.


You'll be confident supporting people to develop their independence, make informed choices and work towards their individual goals. You'll also be able to work independently, use your initiative and contribute positively as part of a team.


A Level 2 or Level 3 qualification in Health and Social Care, or equivalent, would be desirable. Additional qualifications or accredited training in mental health, substance use or recovery support would also be beneficial.


You'll also have:


  • The ability to motivate, encourage and advocate for people using services.
  • Good listening and interpersonal skills, with the ability to communicate effectively at all levels.
  • The ability to respond compassionately to sensitive and complex situations.
  • Strong organisational skills, with the ability to plan and prioritise your workload.
  • Good IT skills, including experience using Microsoft Word, databases and email.
  • The ability to maintain accurate records and handle confidential information appropriately.
  • A commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion.
  • A commitment to your own personal and professional development.
  • Personal and professional integrity, with an understanding of appropriate boundaries.
  • A flexible approach to working, with the ability to meet the needs of the service and the people we support.

Previous experience of working with vulnerable people or individuals with complex needs would be beneficial, as would experience supporting people to develop greater independence.


You must also be flexible and willing to work occasional evenings, nights and weekends when required to meet the needs of the service.


Who will you be working with?


You'll be part of a supportive team, working alongside colleagues and professionals to ensure people receive the right support to achieve their goals.


You'll also build positive working relationships with external agencies, community mental health teams, multidisciplinary professionals and carers, helping to ensure individuals can access the support and resources they need.


Together, you'll contribute to a positive and inclusive working environment, sharing knowledge and expertise to deliver high-quality, person-centred support.


To view the full Job Description CLICK HERE

What We Offer

We value the people who make a difference every day. Alongside meaningful work, you’ll enjoy a comprehensive benefits package:

  • 27 days’ annual leave, rising to 32 after 1 year (plus bank holidays)

  • Pension scheme with 4.5% employer contribution, matched up to 6.5%

  • Life assurance (3× annual salary)

  • Enhanced sick pay and family-friendly pay

  • Birthday leave and the option to buy up to 5 extra days’ annual leave

  • Professional fee reimbursement for relevant qualifications

  • 24/7 online GP access and Employee Assistance Programme

  • Free will writing service and wellbeing initiatives throughout the year

Inclusion and accessibility

Waythrough is proud to be an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and communities, especially those with lived experience of the issues we support.

We have signed up to the Disability Confident Scheme - all applicants are welcome, and adjustments can be made to enable fair participation.

title: Knowledge Specialist - FS Funds
description:
With over 1,600 people situated in key business and financial centres across Europe, the Middle East, Asia and the US, we are an international law firm that acts as a business partner.

Main duties and responsibilities


The successful candidate will be responsible for supporting the PSL to deliver knowhow and professional support services to the London FS Funds team, including:

• Assisting with knowledge management projects generally, both in relation to the FS group as well as in relation to the FMD and the firm in general.


Person specification


Education / qualifications / experience:


• Law graduate with a first or upper second class degree or equivalent.

• This role may well be suited to a law graduate awaiting commencement of a training contract.


Knowledge and technical skills:


The job holder must have the following skills and knowledge:


Service

• Delivers high quality service and seeks to meet and exceed expectations

• Builds and maintains co-operative relationships with others in order to provide a quality service

• Client-focussed, aligns service to the needs of lawyers and clients of the firm


Commercial

• Ability to write legal articles, abstracts and commentaries

• Sound awareness of the UK legal system


Expertise

• A demonstrated understanding of legal concepts and the law generally

• Makes use of information, online databases and knowledge resources effectively

• Can digest, consolidate and analyse information for sharing with colleagues


Here at Simmons & Simmons


Simmons & Simmons is a place where dynamic minds thrive. Our culture is built on work that matters, you will work on inspirational and thought-provoking projects, using your influence to create positive impact for our clients, society and the planet. We also ensure that everyone’s voice is heard from day one, irrespective of job title, qualification, or background. Through innovative learning and development opportunities, you will be provided with a platform to excel, enabling you to exceed your career ambitions and do things you never thought were possible.


Key Highlights:


• Competitive compensation package, (including bonuses dependent on role/level), private medical insurance, and pension contribution.

• A global skills academy offering extensive learning opportunities for all employees.

• A hybrid working model, requiring a minimum of three days in-office, subject to role and client needs.

• Integration of traditional legal expertise with innovative Simmons & Simmons Solutions.

• Recognition as a Stonewall Top Global Employer and a Top 75 Employer for Social Mobility.

• Vibrant social and sports committees, as well as art collections featuring renowned artists.

• The introduction of a Strategic Advisory Council to drive strategic initiatives in line with our mission.


Equal opportunities


We foster an inclusive environment, offering equal employment opportunities across all spectrums of race, ethnicity, religion, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, and more. Requests for flexible working arrangements are supported (where possible), and we strive to make our roles accessible to all. Our employee networks offer additional support, detailed in our D&I Information booklet provided during the recruitment process.


We value diversity and encourage applications from those who are passionate and willing to grow with us, even if not all requirements are met. Your unique experiences and perspectives are welcomed here.


For more information or to apply, please contact our Recruitment Team or visit our career page.

title: Drawing Office Civils Design Lead
description:
Job Title: Drawing Office Civils Design Lead

Location: Cambuslang

Salary + benefits: From £63,200 to £79,000 + Upto 15 % Bonus + Medical Cover



Help us create a better future, quicke


At SP Energy Networks, we are strengthening our Drawing Office capability to support the safe, consistent and efficient delivery of Transmission Network projects. As our Drawing Office Civils Design Lead, you will report to the Drawing Office Manager and take charge of the Civils Drawing Office team. You will manage the team's people, workload, development and delivery. You will also provide technical direction for the production, coordination, checking and quality of civil and structural 3D models and drawings. Your work will help deliver the network that supports Scotland's net zero goals.



What you'll be doing


You will manage the Civils Drawing Office team and provide expert guidance across all civil and structural 3D models and drawings. This includes relevant underground cable civil works within the team's scope. You will combine line management with workload planning, staff development and quality assurance. This ensures every piece of Drawing Office information is controlled and properly assured before issue.


Your day-to-day responsibilities will include:


  • Directing the Civils Drawing Office team, setting clear priorities and maintaining high standards of delivery and quality.
  • Planning and allocating work across the team, balancing project demand, available resource, programme requirements and delivery risk.
  • Providing technical direction so that civil and structural 3D models and drawings are well defined, coordinated, checked and assured.
  • Managing direct reports, including performance, attendance, wellbeing, conduct and development, with support from the Drawing Office Manager.
  • Overseeing recruitment, coaching, mentoring and structured development to build the capability of each team member and of the team as a whole.
  • Promoting the use of BIM, Revit, Autodesk Forma and other digital tools, and embedding agreed standards and workflows.
  • Applying engineering standards, Drawing Office procedures, health and safety requirements, quality controls and design-change arrangements consistently. You will use errors, rework and audit findings to drive practical improvement.
  • Developing and reviewing Drawing Office processes, model and drawing standards and working practices to improve how we produce and deliver information.
  • Coordinating interfaces with Plant, Protection and Control, Cables, Estates, Land and Planning, project teams and external design houses.
  • Keeping the Drawing Office Manager, project teams and stakeholders informed on workload, priorities, technical issues, programme risk and team performance.



What you'll bring


Qualifications and requirements


  • An HNC/HND, degree or equivalent qualification in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering or a closely related discipline. Demonstrable equivalent experience in civil or structural design is also welcome.
  • Demonstrable experience producing civil or structural 3D models and drawings.
  • Demonstrable experience in the technical checking of these models and drawings, with the ability to oversee and assure the quality of Drawing Office outputs.
  • Demonstrable experience managing and coordinating a technical Drawing Office or design-production team. Previous formal line-management experience is desirable but not essential.
  • A UK driving licence and the ability to travel to project and site locations as needed.

Skills and experience


  • Experience producing, coordinating and checking civil and/or structural 3D models and drawings. This may include civil layouts and details, foundations, buildings and structural elements, site infrastructure, and underground cable civil works.
  • Experience in electrical substation civil and structural work is desirable.
  • Experience allocating work, providing technical guidance, helping team members develop and maintaining delivery and quality standards within a design team.
  • A sound knowledge of controlled model and drawing production, checking and change-management processes.
  • Good knowledge of constructability, health and safety requirements, and the application of Drawing Office procedures and engineering standards.
  • The ability to manage multiple priorities, assess complex information, identify interfaces and risks, and give practical direction.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to guide technical discussions, give clear direction and build strong working relationships with internal teams, external design organisations and the supply chain.
  • Experience with 2D and 3D design and information-management tools, including AutoCAD and Revit. Experience with BIM and digital design workflows, including Autodesk Forma, Vault and ProjectWise, is desirable.



What's in it for you


As well as an attractive salary which is reviewed annually, you can also enjoy a number of other benefits. With our pension scheme, we'll double match your contribution up to a company contribution of 10%.

At ScottishPower, we believe it's the little things we do in life that make a big difference. From helping you look after your family's wellbeing, save for your future and take personal steps for climate action -- our benefits are designed to help you do just that - so that you have everything you need to take care of your world -- today and tomorrow. That's why our benefits include:


  • 36 days annual leave
  • Holiday Purchase - perfect your work/life balance with extra annual leave
  • Equity Plans
  • Payroll Giving and Charity Matched Funding
  • Technology Vouchers - save more and spread the cost of your technology purchases
  • Electric Vehicle Schemes - to help you transition to green/clean driving
  • Cycle to Work scheme and Public Transport Season Ticket Loans
  • Healthcare benefit options including: Dental Insurance, Private Medical Insurance, Health Cash Plan and annual Health Assessments
  • Life Assurance (4x salary)
  • Access to Savesmart financial wellbeing assistance
  • Plus shopping, leisure, restaurant and gym discounts, and unique employee deals on travel insurance and more



Why SP Energy Networks


SP Energy Networks is part of the Iberdrola Group, one of the world's largest integrated utility companies and a world leader in wind energy. We keep electricity flowing to homes and businesses through Central and Southern Scotland, North Wales and in the North West of England. We operate over 4000km of cables and lines that make-up the transmission network - connecting infrastructure like wind farms into the electricity system. It's a role that puts us right at the heart of Scotland's goal to be Net Zero by 2044. And we're taking it very seriously. We're investing >£5.5 billion into our transmission network, directly supporting the rapid growth needed in renewable energy. With diverse opportunities across our businesses and a commitment to invest in our own internal talent, ScottishPower can offer people real career opportunities that meet personal and professional goals, in a global organisation.


Inclusion, diversity, and a social purpose are at the heart of everything we do. Alongside our values, they make us a stronger, more sustainable business with direct links to the communities we serve. It takes all sorts of people to build a large-scale business like ours, so whatever your background, you'll fit right in.


We are committed to providing reasonable support or adjustments in our recruiting processes for candidates with disabilities, long term conditions, mental health conditions, or who are neurodivergent or require pregnancy-related support. If you need support, please reach out to careers@scottishpower.com.

title: Senior Structural Analyst
description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of the Blue Origin Engines business unit, where our focus is the design, development, manufacturing, and testing of engines and propulsion systems. Built for multiple uses, our family of engines is powering the next generation of rockets for commercial, civil, national security, and human spaceflight.

Special Mentions

  • Relocation provided
  • Interviews will include a technical assessment
  • Multiple positions available

Role Overview:

Blue Origin is seeking a dedicated and experienced Senior Structural Analyst with expertise in turbomachinery hardware and experience working in ANSYS Workbench. This position plays a vital role in ensuring the structural integrity and reliability of BE-4 turbomachinery components, focusing particularly on the turbomachinery components and subsystems. The successful candidate will possess extensive knowledge in turbomachinery hardware, including both rotating and static hardware (turbine, stator, shafts, flanges, bolted joints, Bladed hardware, housings, etc..) covering strength, fatigue, fracture, modal, and random vibration analysis. Additionally, the candidate should be skilled in constructing free body diagrams to aid in structural evaluations. Collaborating closely with the design team, you will help refine and enhance future configurations through drawing and design requirements.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • ANSYS Workbench: Utilize your expertise in ANSYS Workbench to conduct comprehensive Finite Element Analyses (FEM), including, but not limited to, strength, fatigue, fracture, modal, and random vibration assessments on turbomachinery hardware.
  • Free Body Diagram Construction: Construct and interpret free body diagrams to effectively analyze and solve structural challenges.
  • Structural Command Media and Non-Conformance Assessment: Apply your understanding of Blue Origin’s structural command media to assess non-conformances on the BE-4 Main Turbopump components.
  • Technical Evaluation: Review spin-start component and assembly drawings, providing feedback to ensure designs adhere to Blue Origin’s engineering, safety and performance standards.
  • Design Modifications: Recommend and implement design modifications based on structural analysis results to improve performance and reliability.
  • Cross-Disciplinary Collaboration: Engage with design teams, project managers, and other engineering disciplines to ensure structural considerations are incorporated into the released definition of turbomachinery hardware, and subsequent iterations. Additionally work with Dynamic Environment & System teams to review and incorporate flight responses into the structural evaluations and life assessments.
  • Leadership and Mentorship: Will Play a key role in helping with the development of process / best practice guidelines, and provide technical leadership / help skill development for the rest of the engineering team.

Qualifications

  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work effectively within a collaborative team environment.
  • Excellent communication skills for presenting complex data and recommendations to stakeholders.
  • Excellent Technical writing and documentation of results and rationale
  • Experience in reviewing technical drawings and providing structural input for design modifications.
  • Proven expertise in ANSYS Workbench and advanced understanding of strength, fatigue, fracture (NASGRO), modal, and random vibration analysis.
  • Ability to adapt existing analysis and problem solving skills to assess non-conforming hardware and establish the appropriate rationale for production flight hardware (Scrap, Use As Is, Repair etc…).
  • Adept in constructing free body diagrams to facilitate structural evaluations.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.
  • Previous experience in the Aerospace, Rocket and/or a similar high-technology industry.
  • Knowledge and expertise in Turbopump & turbomachinery hardware.


Base Pay Range for:

WA applicants is $145,188.00 - $203,263.20

Other site ranges may differ

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Benefits

Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details.

title: Head of Development
description:
We are seeking an experienced and commercially driven Head of Development to lead, grow and manage our Infrastructure Development business across the Middle East, providing strategic leadership across development management, infrastructure and multidisciplinary pre-construction services.

The role will position the business as a trusted strategic adviser, turning client investment objectives into commercially viable, deliverable projects from early engagement through to delivery. It holds accountability for the Development P&L and for building a high-performing multidisciplinary team aligned with market demand.

Business Leadership and Strategy

  • Define and deliver the Middle East Development strategy and annual business plan, aligned with regional sector priorities.

  • Establish an integrated market proposition spanning development management, design, infrastructure and advisory services.

  • Champion a sector-first, client-led approach, focusing on priority clients, programmes and geographies with the strongest commercial potential.

  • Monitor market trends, competitor activity and client investment plans, adapting the strategy and service offering accordingly.

Client Care and Key Account Leadership

  • Build trusted relationships with senior clients, investors, developers and government entities, acting as executive sponsor for priority accounts.

  • Establish structured key-account plans covering relationship mapping, engagement priorities, opportunity pipelines and account-growth objectives.

  • Actively seek client feedback and intervene early where satisfaction, project performance or commercial relationships are at risk.

  • Ensure clients experience one integrated business, using successful outcomes to secure repeat and adjacent work.

Winning Work and Market Growth

  • Own a qualified pipeline sufficient to meet revenue and growth targets, applying disciplined bid/no-bid decisions.

  • Develop capture strategies well ahead of procurement, positioning the business for sole-source appointments, frameworks and follow-on services.

  • Lead major pursuits, shaping the win strategy, value proposition, team, fee and commercial position.

  • Track pipeline value, probability, sales stage and conversion, and represent the business at senior client and industry forums.

P&L and Commercial Accountability

  • Own the Development P&L, including orders, revenue, margin, utilisation, working capital and cash collection.

  • Manage the annual budget and rolling forecast, taking early corrective action on variances.

  • Ensure fees, scope, resourcing and risk are robustly reviewed before contractual commitment, with commercial, finance and legal teams.

  • Provide commercial oversight of major projects, including change control, cost-to-complete and debt management.

  • Make balanced investment decisions and promote a culture of commercial ownership among project leaders.

Resource and Capability Management

  • Maintain a strategic resource plan aligned with secured workload and pipeline, balancing utilisation, project needs and employee wellbeing.

  • Address capacity constraints and skill gaps, leading recruitment and mobilising regional and global expertise.

  • Build a scalable operating model with clear roles, accountabilities and decision rights.

  • Develop succession plans and hold the leadership team accountable for client service, delivery, financial performance and people development.

Development Leadership and Multidisciplinary Integration

  • Provide executive leadership for major development programmes from inception through planning, design, approvals and transition into delivery.

  • Translate client aspirations and investment objectives into clear briefs, strategies and delivery plans.

  • Ensure effective mobilisation and controls, while empowering project leaders to manage day-to-day delivery.

  • Integrate master planning, architecture, infrastructure, transport, sustainability and specialist disciplines early, balancing placemaking, commercial viability and deliverability.

Governance, Leadership and Culture

  • Maintain effective governance and assurance across the portfolio, actively managing material contractual, financial, technical and reputational risks.

  • Ensure major bids and projects receive appropriate executive review, with issues escalated early.

  • Provide clear, visible and inclusive leadership, communicating strategy, priorities and expected standards.

  • Build a culture of client care, commercial ownership, collaboration and integrity, coaching senior team members as client leaders and work winners.

Key Performance Outcomes

  • Achievement of agreed orders, revenue, margin, utilisation, working-capital and cash targets, supported by accurate forecasting.

  • A strong, qualified and well-balanced pipeline, with improved conversion of priority pursuits.

  • Growth in repeat, sole-source and multidisciplinary commissions, with high client satisfaction across priority accounts.

  • Effective mobilisation and delivery of major commissions, with consistent governance and risk management.

  • Appropriate capacity, capability and talent retention, with strong collaboration across sectors and geographies.

  • Typically 15+ years’ experience, including senior leadership in development management, master planning, multidisciplinary design or programme management in the Middle East.

  • Proven P&L accountability, including business planning, revenue, margin, forecasting, utilisation, working capital and investment decisions.

  • Strong track record of senior client relationships and winning major, complex commissions.

  • Strong understanding of development economics, approvals, procurement and delivery interfaces, with sound commercial awareness.

  • Degree in architecture, engineering, planning, real estate or a related discipline; professional or chartered status is advantageous.

  • Demonstrable experience leading large-scale, complex developments or infrastructure programmes through feasibility, business case, planning, design, procurement and delivery readiness.

  • Established network and market credibility with major developers, investors, government authorities and delivery partners across the Middle East, with the ability to originate and convert opportunities.

  • Experience building and leading high-performing multidisciplinary teams across multiple locations, including workforce planning, recruitment, succession planning and leadership development.

  • Strong knowledge of regional development and procurement models, consultant appointments, contractual risk, commercial governance and the management of joint ventures or strategic delivery partnerships.

Join our close-knit community of talented individuals who share your passion for making a positive impact. Our global team includes more than 69,000 employees, working together to make a difference in communities both close to home and around the world.

title: Senior Specialist Market Access
description:
Job Description

We are seeking a highly motivated Senior Specialist, Market Access to support reimbursement, pricing, and access activities across Serbia, Bosnia & Herzegovina, and Montenegro. In this role, you will lead the preparation and submission of market access files, support pricing strategy and negotiations, and contribute to the successful launch and lifecycle management of our portfolio, with full pricing responsibility for the Oncology portfolio in the three markets.

This is a strategic and cross-functional role requiring strong analytical capability, stakeholder management, and deep understanding of local healthcare and reimbursement environments.


Key Responsibilities:


Reimbursement and Access Submissions

  • Lead and coordinate the preparation, compilation, and submission of reimbursement and access dossiers for products across Serbia, Bosnia & Herzegovina, and Montenegro, ensuring compliance with local requirements and internal standards.
  • Ensure all submission packages are complete, accurate, strategically positioned, and submitted within agreed timelines.
  • Coordinate cross-functional input for submissions, including medical, epidemiological, pharmacoeconomic, pricing, regulatory, and commercial components.
  • Prepare and adapt value dossiers, briefing materials, and submission documents for local authorities and expert bodies.
  • Monitor the progress of submitted files and support responses to follow-up questions, clarification requests, and requests for additional data from authorities.
  • Maintain accurate archives and tracking of submitted files, decisions, timelines, and supporting rationale.

Market Access Materials and Strategic Positioning

  • Lead the creation and regular update of MYMI and other key internal market access materials to ensure robust and consistent strategic positioning of products.
  • Ensure MYMI content reflects the local access environment, payer expectations, competitive dynamics, and portfolio priorities across the three countries.
  • Collaborate with global, regional, and local stakeholders to align brand strategy, pricing assumptions, evidence generation plans, and reimbursement goals.
  • Develop additional access-supporting materials, including value stories, negotiation decks, product positioning summaries, and stakeholder-specific materials as needed.

Negotiations and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Prepare financial and access offers in line with internal governance, market access strategy, and local payer expectations.
  • Actively participate in negotiations with relevant healthcare authorities and institutions, supporting the achievement of optimal reimbursement and access outcomes.
  • Build and maintain effective professional relationships with key external stakeholders involved in reimbursement and access decision-making.
  • Work closely with scientific leaders from REC and CDC to support scientific alignment, understanding of clinical value, and appropriate positioning of company products within local treatment pathways and access frameworks.
  • Support preparation of meeting materials, negotiation arguments, response documents, and follow-up actions related to payer and expert discussions.

Pricing Responsibility

  • Hold full pricing responsibility for the Oncology portfolio in Serbia, Bosnia & Herzegovina, and Montenegro.
  • Lead pricing analyses, pricing proposals, and internal approval processes in accordance with global pricing policies and local legal frameworks.
  • Prepare and submit pricing files and documentation required by local authorities for oncology products.
  • Assess pricing implications of external reference pricing, comparator movements, reimbursement conditions, and market events, and provide recommendations to internal stakeholders.
  • Support pricing strategy for the full portfolio, ensuring consistency between pricing, reimbursement, and business priorities.

Tender and Portfolio Support

  • Support the development and execution of tender strategies across the full portfolio in collaboration with commercial, access, and leadership teams.
  • Provide market access and pricing input into tender decisions, discounting approaches, offer construction, and account-specific access considerations.
  • Contribute to portfolio prioritization by assessing feasibility, access barriers, timing, payer dynamics, and resource requirements across products and markets.
  • Partner with relevant colleagues to ensure that tender, pricing, reimbursement, and contracting activities are aligned and mutually supportive.

Cross-Functional and Strategic Support

  • Work in close partnership with Medical, Commercial, Finance, Policy, Regulatory, and Global/Regional Access teams to ensure integrated execution of market access priorities.
  • Provide strategic input into portfolio planning, launch preparation, evidence needs, timeline development, and risk assessment.
  • Track relevant policy, reimbursement, pricing, and committee developments in Serbia, Bosnia & Herzegovina, and Montenegro, and translate them into business implications and recommended actions.
  • Support management in preparing updates, strategic reviews, and decision-making materials related to market access opportunities and challenges.

Qualifications:


  • University degree in Medicine, Pharmacy, Economics, or a related field.
  • Relevant experience in Market Access, Pricing, Reimbursement, Health Economics, Tendering, or External Affairs within the pharmaceutical industry.
  • Strong understanding of the healthcare systems, reimbursement pathways, and pricing environment in Serbia, Bosnia & Herzegovina, and Montenegro.
  • Experience preparing reimbursement/access files, working with healthcare authorities, and supporting negotiation processes.
  • Experience in pricing strategy and pricing approvals.
  • Strong understanding of pharmaceutical legislation, reimbursement frameworks, payer environment, and market access requirements.
  • Ability to work effectively with scientific experts, payers, and cross-functional internal teams.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and project management skills.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Fluent in English and Serbian.
  • Strong PC skills; advanced knowledge of Excel and PowerPoint, and experience working with structured submission documents is an advantage.
  • Ability to balance strategic thinking with operational execution across multiple markets and priorities.
  • Oncology experience is a strong advantage.

What We Offer:


  • An opportunity to shape market access strategy across multiple countries.
  • A highly collaborative, cross-functional environment.
  • Exposure to strategic pricing, reimbursement, and tender activities.
  • The chance to contribute to improved patient access to innovative therapies.

Additional location(s) Compensation Information:

Required Skills:

Cost Effectiveness Analysis, Healthcare Reimbursement, Health Economics, Health Technology Assessment (HTA), Market Access, Oncology, Pricing Management

title: Data Product Owner
description:
Join the change. Electrify your future!

We've been proudly Aussie since 1837, always finding new ways to innovate in energy and essential services. Now, we're moving towards a sustainable future through electrification and investing in renewable energy—and we’d like you to join us. Whether you're on-site, in the office, or somewhere in between, you'll find opportunities to grow your career here. You'll work with a team that's passionate about powering Australian lives, in a culture that values inclusivity, respect, and learning. Help us create a cleaner energy future, and we’ll back you every step of the way as you build your career.

Join the change. Electrify your future.

About the role


Join AGL's Asset Intelligence team as a Data Product Owner. You will own the business meaning, quality, usability, adoption, governance and lifecycle of assigned Energy Assets data products, helping ensure they are trusted, discoverable, reusable and aligned to operational priorities.

Working across the business and technology landscape, you will combine strong Databricks capability and data governance expertise with practical stakeholder engagement to turn complex data needs into clear, valuable product outcomes.


What you'll be doing


  • Own and continuously improve the vision, roadmap, priorities and success measures for assigned Energy Assets data products.
  • Embed strong data governance across products built on the EDP (Databricks) platform, including business definitions, metadata, lineage, data quality rules, access expectations and lifecycle controls.
  • Partner with business leaders, data owners, SMEs and consumers to translate operational priorities into clear product outcomes, requirements and acceptance criteria.
  • Prioritise product backlogs, enhancements, data quality improvements and issue remediation based on value, risk, urgency and business impact.
  • Work closely with Data Engineering, Architecture, Technology and platform teams to deliver secure, scalable and reusable data products, supporting ETL, migration, reconciliation, validation and release readiness.

About You


You are an established data leader who can connect business priorities, governance expectations and technology delivery. You bring strong hands-on experience with Databricks and enterprise data governance, and you are confident engaging stakeholders across operational and technical teams to build alignment and drive adoption. A consulting background would be ideal, particularly if you have experience turning complex business problems into practical, governed data product outcomes.

What you'll bring to the table


  • Strong hands-on experience with Databricks or a comparable enterprise data platform, including building, governing, cataloguing and enabling reusable data products for business consumption.
  • Demonstrated expertise in data governance and data management, including ownership, stewardship, metadata, lineage, data quality, access controls and lifecycle management.
  • Proven ability to engage business stakeholders, facilitate decisions and translate operational needs into clear product roadmaps, requirements, priorities and acceptance criteria.
  • Working knowledge of ETL and data migration practices, including profiling, cleansing, source-to-target mapping, transformation, reconciliation, validation and business acceptance.
  • Experience working across business SMEs, data stewards, engineers, architects, analysts, platform teams and governance specialists; relevant tertiary qualifications or equivalent professional experience are highly regarded.

title: Manager, Financial Planning & Analysis
location: Polaris Pharmacy Services of Ft Lauderdale - Ft. Lauderdale, FL 33309
description:
Position Overview

Manager of Financial Planning & Analysis partners with the Vice President of Strategic Finance, the CFO, and operational leaders in driving financial visibility, operational performance, and long-term value creation.

The core of this role is owning and leading Polaris's planning cycle: the annual operating plan, the quarterly reforecast, and the long-range plan. The Manager will also own monthly performance reporting and KPI development, and will build the financial models that help leadership translate operational initiatives into measurable financial outcomes. The role has one direct report, a Financial Analyst, with the team expected to evolve as the function grows.

Cash Forecasting & Lender Reporting

  • Develop and maintain the 13-week cash flow forecast, providing visibility into liquidity and funding needs in collaboration with treasury lead
  • Support working capital analysis, including AR, inventory, and payables, to improve cash conversion
  • Prepare financial analyses supporting lender reporting, covenant compliance calculations, and financing activities as needed

Team Leadership

  • Supervise, coach, and develop one direct report (Financial Analyst), with the team expected to evolve as the function grows; review work product for accuracy and quality
  • Document FP&A processes and continuously improve tools, templates, and timelines, including integrating AI into planning and reporting workflows

Annual Plan, Quarterly Reforecast & Long-Range Plan (Core of the Role)

  • Own and lead the company's annual operating plan end to end, including the planning calendar, assumptions, templates, and coordination with pharmacy site and functional leaders
  • Own and lead the quarterly reforecast, updating the full-year outlook for revenue, gross margin, EBITDA, and cash, and explaining changes versus plan
  • Own and lead the long-range plan, linking it to Polaris's strategic priorities, growth initiatives, and capital needs
  • Build site-level plans and forecasts for each pharmacy and infusion center that roll up to the consolidated plan
  • Present the annual plan, quarterly reforecasts, and long-range plan to the VP of Strategic Finance and CFO, and prepare materials for executive and board review

Performance Management & KPI Development

  • Maintain enterprise and site-level KPI frameworks and performance metrics
  • Prepare monthly budget-vs-actual and forecast variance analysis, explaining drivers of revenue, gross margin, and EBITDA

  • Contribute to periodic (monthly/quarterly) financial accounting processes, maintaining accurate and complete supplier PO information.
  • Serve as counterpart for key clinical trial suppliers with respect to financial oversight working across the Amgen portfolio.
  • Maintain relationships with key suppliers to ensure process alignment, status updates and timely issue management.
  • Communicates, resolves, and tracks PO budget-related questions between Finance Operations and Clinical Trial teams
  • Maintains materials for project financial review meetings with Clinical study teams.
  • Maintain PO accuracy and compliance with Amgen policies
  • Maintain PO and SOW documentation in central repositories (e.g. TMF) and ensure audit/readiness standards are met.
  • Oversee timely review and approval of invoices in Amgen ERP system to ensure on time payments
  • Manage and resolve issues related to supplier invoices and payments in partnership with invoice approvers and Amgen AP
  • Maintain PO tracking (dashboard/log) and deliver regular PO status reports.
  • Monitor PO-related supplier delivery and identify PO risks; share issues with manager and Supplier Governance Leads for oversight and escalation.
  • Ensure PO activities align with GCP, company procurement policies and clinical trial requirements.

Key Activities

  • PO lifecycle management
    • Review SOWs to confirm compliance with Amgen purchasing standards.
    • Prepare and submit PO and funding requests through the enterprise procurement/P2P system or established finance workflow; follow up until submission confirmation.
    • Manage PO amendments and change orders to reflect scope changes.

  • PO submission & tracking
    • Submit POs via the enterprise procurement/P2P or finance workflow and maintain a PO tracking dashboard showing submission, routing/approvals, funding status, and closure targets.
    • Proactively chase routing/processing issues and escalate blockers to the Manager or Supplier Governance Leads
    • Analyze PO related data support optimized processing times and quality
    • Communicate on a regular basis with supplier and Amgen stakeholders regarding progress of pending PO requests and to monitor PO budgets

  • Financial stewardship (scope limited to PO spend tracking)
    • Perform ongoing budget reviews and track commitments against PO balances; identify variances and forecast spend related to active clinical supplier POs.
    • Provide accurate and complete supplier PO information to support financial accrual and forecasting processes
    • Perform data QC to ensure accuracy of data in source systems
    • Use data analysis to investigate issues, answer study budget related queries

  • Supplier oversight & issue coordination
    • Monitor supplier delivery versus PO/SOW milestones and summarize PO-related risks for stakeholders.
    • Communicate with supplier and study teams to review PO, invoice, and PO budgets topics
    • Independently manage and resolve issues related to SoW, PO and invoices to support clinical trial execution and budget management.
    • Manage multiple priorities, balancing study delivery and budgetary controls to ensure timely execution of SoW/POs and timely invoice approval.
    • Ensure PO/SOW linkage to TMF and central repositories is maintained and audit-ready.

description:

title: Resident Service Coordinator - Providence Gardens
description:
Who We Are

Redwood Communities, Inc. (“Redwood Communities”), an affiliate of Redwood Housing, is a multifamily property management organization that manages affordable housing communities throughout the country. To date, Redwood Communities has assembled a best-in-class team that currently manages a growing portfolio of properties and has built strong working relationships with government agencies and leading non-profit organizations to raise the standard of living for our communities.

Benefits

  • Exceptional medical benefits: We cover more than 90% of medical premiums, and employees have the option of a 100% employer-paid HSA medical plan.
  • 100% company paid dental and vision benefits for employee coverage.
  • Healthcare and dependent care flexible spending accounts.
  • Company paid life insurance, AD&D
  • Best-in-class voluntary insurance benefits.
  • Pre-tax and Roth 401(k) programs with a company match equal to 100% of the first 6% contributed by the employee.
  • Employee assistance program (EAP) with 24/7 counseling services.
  • 3 weeks of paid time off each year.
  • 12 paid holidays each year & 2 floating holidays.

About the Position

The Resident Services Coordinator (RSC) helps residents access services, strengthen housing stability, and remain as independent and self-reliant as possible. The RSC assesses non-clinical needs, coordinates referrals and supportive services, develops community partnerships and resident programming, and maintains accurate, secure, and timely documentation. The role works proactively with residents, property teams, community partners, supervisors, and leadership while respecting resident choice, dignity, privacy, and individual goals.

Schedule: Monday-Friday 8am-5pm

Pay Details: $26.50-$28.50/hour

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Resident Support & Advocacy:

  • Serve as a connector, coordinator, educator, advocate, and documenter for residents while maintaining clear professional boundaries.
  • Maintain a visible, proactive presence with clear office hours and ongoing professional relationships with residents.
  • Conduct resident intake and non-clinical assessments to identify priorities, risks, strengths, activities of daily living, and service needs without diagnosing.
  • Develop or update resident services plans collaboratively with participating residents; respect and document a resident’s decision to decline participation.
  • Provide general or limited case management when appropriate and when the needed service is not otherwise available through the larger service community.
  • Assist residents in accessing public benefits and supportive resources, including food, health coverage, income supports, energy assistance, transportation, and other locally available services.
  • Make referrals with resident permission, obtain signed consent before sharing protected information, and follow up to determine whether services were timely, appropriate, and responsive to the resident’s need.
  • Advocate and, when appropriate, negotiate on behalf of residents for adequate, timely, and cost-effective services while avoiding unhealthy dependence.

Program Development and Community Partnerships

  • Develop and coordinate educational, wellness, prevention, employment-readiness, and community-engagement activities based on identified resident needs.
  • Coordinate on-site services, screenings, clinics, workshops, speakers, volunteer opportunities, resident meetings, resource fairs, and community-building activities.
  • Build productive relationships with local, state, and federal agencies, nonprofit organizations, service providers, and volunteer groups.
  • Maintain a current resource directory that identifies who each provider serves, referral procedures, consent requirements, follow-up steps, and options when access barriers arise; update it at least annually and whenever provider information changes.
  • Identify service gaps, pursue additional resources, and elevate barriers that limit resident access or program effectiveness.
  • Strengthen informal support networks among residents and with families, as appropriate and with resident consent.

Documentation, Privacy and Reporting

  • Maintain complete, objective, prompt, organized, and secure resident case files consistent with HUD requirements and company policy.
  • Document intake information, assessments, services plans, resident contacts, referrals, consent, participation or refusal, follow-up, progress notes, and disposition or termination of services in the approved case-management system.
  • Maintain program records, including training documentation, reports, provider agreements, program files, eligible expense records, and other required supporting documentation.
  • If applicable, prepare accurate internal and HUD-required reports, including the HUD Multifamily Housing Service Coordinator Program Annual Report (HUD Form 92456).
  • Protect resident privacy and share resident-specific information only when authorized, necessary, and consistent with HUD, HIPAA, Fair Housing, organizational confidentiality, consent, and records-security requirements.
  • Take immediate action to correct missing, late, inaccurate, or insecure documentation and participate in file reviews and quality-assurance activities.

Communication, Collaboration and Escalation

  • Maintain strong communication and collaboration with property staff, supervisors, service providers, and quality assurance partners to address resident needs, service gaps, risks, and housing stability concerns.
  • Work closely with property management while appropriately referring leasing, rent collection, maintenance, and enforcement matters to their team, and coordinating interventions for residents at risk of eviction or housing instability.
  • Promptly escalate safety, abuse, neglect, or legal concerns according to protocol, while meeting all training, reporting, documentation, and professional responsiveness requirements.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Complete at least 36 hours of initial training before hiring or within 12 months of the initial hire date. Topics include aging, federal and state programs, elder and disability services, legal liability, substance use, and mental health.
  • Knowledge of HUD Multifamily housing programs, Section 8, service coordinator funding requirements, Fair Housing, reasonable accommodations, and confidentiality obligations.
  • Knowledge of older-adult and disability services, supportive housing, public benefits, local resources, referral processes, and federal and state entitlement programs.
  • Ability to conduct non-clinical assessments, facilitate services, organize programs, solve problems, advocate effectively, and achieve documented results.
  • Excellent interpersonal, written, presentation, organization, follow-up, and professional communication skills.
  • Cultural competency and bilingual skills when relevant to the resident population.
  • Ability to work independently, prioritize competing needs, maintain professional boundaries, and use sound judgment in standardized and urgent situations.
  • Intermediate proficiency with Microsoft Windows, Outlook, Word, Excel, Teams, online time keeping and training, shared files, and approved resident or case-management systems.

title: Lead Member Services Officer
description:
If you are motivated and believe in the credit union philosophy of "People Helping People," join our team!

Position Overview

Lead Member Services Officers should have a broad thorough knowledge of all branch operational procedures. Lead MSOs will assist with resolving member issues and complaints across all delivery channels and mentor less experienced staff. Lead MSOs are expected to be leaders in the branch, to manage the branch in the absence of the VP/SVP and ABM, and take a leadership role in loan underwriting, ensuring team member training is completed, and/or collections. They should be willing to assist and supervise in all areas of branch operations.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Enhanced Expectations and Responsibilities at this Position Level*
    • Assist in the management of the branch at the direction of ABM/VP/SVP.
    • Take a leadership role in the branch for one or more of the following:
      • Oversee loan review processes to ensure that loans are underwritten in accordance with SECU policy and that all staff are up to date with lending policies.
      • Supervise the collections process for the branch office at the direction of the ABM/VP/SVP. This would include assisting in all lending and deposit account collection efforts as well as overseeing the lending collection efforts of other staff to ensure that all queues are completed as required by SECU policy.
      • Serve as a mentor for newer staff in all areas of MSO operations. This includes ensuring all necessary training is completed, making sure employees are up to date on new product offerings, and providing support for less experienced staff to ensure compliance.
      • Take leadership role in any other area(s) identified by management
  • Act as a liaison(s) to Loss Mitigation and submit any required reporting of collection efforts conducted by branch staff.
  • Serve as a resource in specialized deposit accounts and survivor relations:
  • Assess member’s current financial condition, help identify short-term goals and priorities, develop a financial improvement plan, and set recurring meetings with the member to monitor progress and make adjustments.
  • Assist members with tax-advantaged (IRAs, HSAs, CESAs, 529 Plans) accounts, demonstrating a thorough understanding of account types, features, and transactional rules/requirements.
  • Assist members and/or fiduciaries with trust and estate deposit accounts, demonstrating a thorough understanding of documentation requirements, account titling parameters, and transactional rules.
  • Assist in all areas of survivor relations – assist family members, beneficiaries, fiduciaries with account management, advise on action needed when presented with a death certificate, etc.
  • Partner with licensed FAS team member to incorporate FAS solutions when necessary to meet members’ needs.
  • Provide support to other team members in this area and ensure proper escalation to FAS when appropriate.
  • Assist MLOs in non-MLO functions. The branch Mortgage Lending Specialist would be responsible for training the Lead MSO in these responsibilities.
  • Performance Expectations and Essential Responsibilities*
    • Comply with all Credit Union policies and regulatory requirements.
    • Ensure all member information remains confidential, and members’ accounts are accessed for business purposes only.
    • Security and control procedures must be followed by all branch employees.
    • Completion of Consumer Lending Program (CLP) courses. Passing score on CLP Exam required prior to becoming a Member Services Officer.
    • The Lead Member Services Officer is granted Tier 5 Lending Limits (As Assigned) at this level and are able to approve loans within those limits.
    • Assist members in all areas of consumer lending. Evaluate loan applications and approve or deny within assigned limits.
    • Review and approve loans within lending limits that are outside the limits of less experienced staff.
    • Contact members and document efforts regarding deposit and/or loan collection reports as directed by management. Ensure all Default Manager queues are clear within the proper timeframes.
    • Serve members by processing transactions in the appropriate system. If requested by Management, this includes balancing a cash drawer in accordance with Performance Measurement Criteria standard.
    • Thorough understanding of SECU Check Acceptance Guidelines and Hold procedures.
    • Greet and assist members in a courteous, professional, and timely manner through all service channels – in-person, phone, and digital communication.
    • Answer phones and assist members with service requests.
    • Assist with balancing automated teller machines, teller cash dispenser, and coin sorter.
    • Assist with evaluating mobile and automated teller machine check deposits as needed.
    • Help verify and prepare cash delivery and shipments as directed by management.
    • Interact with other departments to facilitate member requests.
    • Organize, file and scan documents daily.
    • Process foreign and domestic wires.
    • Proficiency in account maintenance and opening all account types for new members while following MIP procedures.
    • Open and process maintenance on tax advantaged accounts, process foreign and domestic wire transfers, redeem savings bonds, and help order and return foreign currency.
    • Troubleshoot problems with member accounts, cards, and on-line access including processing disputes.
    • Remain up to date on all credit union products in order to educate members on available services and make informed recommendations based on need.
    • Knowledgeable in basic Financial Advisory and Real Estate Services (i.e. insurance, retirement planning, investment services, trust, and mortgage services) and able to provide quality referrals.
    • Review and take appropriate action on negative checking, NSFB, and Share Below $25 report. Contact members and document efforts regarding deposit and/or loan collection reports as assigned. Collection Training class is required prior to collecting loans.
    • Establish and facilitate member safe deposit box access.
    • Perform subsequent advances on existing open and home equity lines of credit.
    • Execute Notary Public Services.

title: Manager, GHG Data Specialist
description:
Role Purpose and Impact

This role contributes to the delivery, evolution and disclosure of LSEG’s Climate Transition Plan.

You will be working in partnership with key stakeholders across Operations, Technology, Procurement, Finance and Group Risk to oversee and drive GHG data collection, quality and disclosure to support our broader climate transition plan and targets.

Key Responsibilities

  • GHG management tool: Lead the day-to-day administration and technical management of the GHG data system. Work with the external provider to ensure the tool works effectively and users have the right access. Identify issues and improvements, regularly review how the system is performing, and support the implementation of a new tool, including the accurate transfer of historical data and correct system set-up.
  • Vendor management: Work with Procurement, Group Sustainability and other relevant teams to agree clear expectations, responsibilities and ways of working with the system provider.   • Controls: Carry out system and data process controls to confirm that reviews are completed, data quality is maintained, and errors are identified, recorded and addressed.
  • Data quality: Complete first-line quality checks on all GHG data. Work with data providers and the climate team to resolve questions and correct issues where needed. Keep clear records of the checks completed, findings and actions taken to support further review.
  • Ongoing remediation: Identify gaps, inconsistencies and control failures in the data. Record them in the data issues log and track the actions needed to resolve them.
  • Stakeholder management: Work with the climate team and GHG data owners to ensure data is collected accurately and on time, supporting complete and reliable submissions.

Technical / job functional knowledge

  • Greenhouse Gas Emissions and/or Carbon accounting experience
  • Strong data management and analytical skills
  • Experience operating a GHG management tool is preferable

Business and sector expertise

  • Strong climate and environmental sustainability experience is essential
  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail required
  • Strong stakeholder relationship skills to develop effective relationships across LSEG as required to perform the role
  • Financial sector experience is beneficial
