About Basecamp Recovery Center

Basecamp Recovery Center (BRC) is a CARF-accredited, Medicaid-funded behavioral health and substance use disorder treatment organization serving the Columbus, Ohio community. At the heart of our mission are our core values: Love, Community, Consistency, Honesty, and Hope. These principles guide how we serve our clients, support one another, and uphold the standards that make Basecamp a trusted place for healing and growth.

Our services include:

  • Outpatient Treatment — Individual and group counseling, evidence-based therapies, and psychiatric support
  • Medication-Assisted Treatment (MAT) — Safe, physician-guided treatment options to support recovery
  • Peer Support Services — Certified Peer Recovery Specialists offering lived-experience guidance and encouragement
  • Case Management — Helping clients connect with housing, employment, and community resources
  • Recovery Housing — Safe and supportive housing for individuals working toward stability and independence

Job Summary

The Site Director leads all clinical and intake services at one Basecamp Recovery Center (BRC) location. This role supervises the site's Clinical Supervisor, clinical staff, and intake team, and is accountable for clinical quality, clinician impact (productivity), intake, documentation, and clinical staffing at the site. The Site Director reports to the Senior Director of Patient & Site Services and works closely with the Director of Operations (pharmacy, facilities, and operations) and the Corporate Compliance Operations Leader (transportation, front desk, and administrative compliance).

Job Duties

CLINICAL LEADERSHIP

  • Lead clinical programming at the site, including groups, individual services, and treatment planning
  • Provide clinical supervision within the scope of the Site Director's own Ohio credential and route anything outside that scope to the Senior Director of Patient & Site Services
  • Supervise the Clinical Supervisor and hold them accountable for documentation timeliness and quality
  • Manage caseload distribution and clinical client flow at the site
  • Lead or participate in case consultation and clinical incident response at the site

CLINICIAN IMPACT (PRODUCTIVITY)

  • Hold each clinician at the site accountable for meeting BRC's monthly impact (billable productivity) target
  • Track impact for every clinician weekly against the monthly target and address shortfalls early, before the month closes
  • Manage scheduling, caseloads, and group assignments so clinicians have the patient volume needed to meet impact
  • Coach clinicians who fall below target and document the plan; partner with Human Resources when a pattern continues
  • Report site and individual clinician impact to the Senior Director of Patient & Site Services each month
  • Confirm that billed services are supported by complete, timely documentation; impact counts only for services that meet billing standards

INTAKE

  • Supervise intake staff at the site, including screening, assessment, and admission
  • Apply BRC intake standards, admission criteria, and level-of-care placement consistently
  • Track time from first contact to admission and follow up on referrals that stall
  • Coordinate intake scheduling and handoffs with clinical, medical, and front desk staff

CLINICAL STAFFING & PEOPLE LEADERSHIP

  • Build and maintain the clinical and intake staffing schedule to meet program and coverage requirements
  • Review and approve direct reports' timecards in Paycom weekly, no later than 12:00 PM (noon) on Monday of each pay week; route any corrections through the employee and document them
  • Recommend hiring, discipline, and separation of clinical and intake staff to the Senior Director of Patient & Site Services and Human Resources, with supporting documentation
  • Complete performance evaluations for direct reports on time
  • Verify required credentials and trainings are complete before new clinical or intake staff work independently

DOCUMENTATION, BILLING & QUALITY

  • Monitor clinical and intake documentation timeliness and quality and correct gaps before they reach billing
  • Support Prior Authorization tracking and escalate at-risk authorizations to the Senior Director of Patient & Site Services
  • Keep clinical and intake records survey-ready for CARF, OhioMHAS, and payer audits
  • Follow 42 CFR Part 2, HIPAA, OhioMHAS, and Ohio Medicaid requirements and report concerns to Corporate Compliance
  • Report incidents, grievances, and employee relations concerns to the appropriate leader and Human Resources within required timeframes

PARTNERSHIP WITH OPERATIONS AND CORPORATE COMPLIANCE

  • Work with the Director of Operations on facilities, supplies, pharmacy, and other operational needs at the site
  • Work with the Corporate Compliance Operations Leader on transportation, front desk, and patient scheduling needs at the site
  • Bring unresolved operational issues to the Senior Director of Patient & Site Services

REPORTING & COMMUNICATION

  • Meet weekly with the Senior Director of Patient & Site Services and report on site clinical and intake KPIs, staffing, and risks
  • Submit a monthly site clinical report covering census, clinician impact, intake, documentation compliance, staffing, and incidents
  • Hold regular clinical team meetings at the site
  • Stay current on all assigned Relias and Trainual trainings within required timeframes
  • Adhere to the BRC Attendance and Punctuality Policy
  • Performs other duties as assigned

Scope and Decision-Making Authority

This role holds clinical and intake leadership authority for one BRC site, within the limits below.

  • Clinical and intake decisions for the assigned site within BRC policy
  • Clinical supervision and decisions within the scope of the incumbent's own Ohio credential
  • Approval of schedules, time-off requests, and timecards for direct reports
  • Recommends hiring, discipline, and separation; final decisions are made with the Senior Director of Patient & Site Services, Human Resources, and the CEO
  • Clinical matters outside the incumbent's licensure go to the Senior Director of Patient & Site Services
  • No authority over operational functions, transportation, front desk, pharmacy, medical practice, or prescribing
  • No independent authority over compensation or policy changes

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

CLINICIAN IMPACT (PRODUCTIVITY)

  • Site meets BRC's monthly clinician impact target, measured as total billable impact across all site clinicians
  • Every clinician below target has a documented coaching plan within 5 business days of month-end
  • Monthly impact report by clinician submitted to the Senior Director of Patient & Site Services by the 5th of each month

DOCUMENTATION & BILLING

  • Clinical documentation completed within BRC's required timeframe at a 95% rate or higher
  • Billing documentation compliance of 95% or higher on internal audits
  • No authorization lapses at the site caused by missed renewal deadlines

INTAKE

  • Time from first contact to admission reported monthly and within the target set by the Senior Director of Patient & Site Services
  • Intake documentation complete and accurate on internal audits at a 95% rate or higher

STAFFING & LEADERSHIP

  • Clinical and intake schedule posted at least 2 weeks in advance, with no uncovered required shifts
  • Direct-report performance evaluations completed on time
  • 100% of direct reports' timecards approved by 12:00 PM (noon) Monday of each pay week

COMPLIANCE & QUALITY

  • Incidents reported within required timeframes
  • No critical clinical or intake findings attributable to the site on CARF, OhioMHAS, or payer audits
  • Active, unrestricted Ohio licensure maintained, with continuing education completed on time

REPORTING

  • Weekly check-in held with the Senior Director of Patient & Site Services
  • Monthly site clinical report submitted by the 5th of each month

title: Full Stack Software Engineer, Associate – Preqin Engineering
description:
About this role

Your team

Preqin, part of BlackRock, is seeking a Full Stack Software Engineer (Associate) to join the London Engineering team. The team develops and supports technology solutions that power Preqin's private markets platform, helping clients access high-quality data, analytics, and workflow capabilities globally. You will work with a collaborative, international engineering team focused on delivering scalable, cloud-first solutions while applying modern software engineering practices across the full product lifecycle.

Your role and impact

As a Full Stack Software Engineer, you will contribute to the design, development, deployment, and support of critical Preqin products. This role offers the opportunity to work across both backend and frontend technologies, with a particular emphasis on building robust services using Python and .NET alongside modern React-based user experiences. You will help drive engineering excellence, contribute to architectural decisions, and support the evolution of products that serve a global client base in the private markets industry.

Your responsibilities

In every role at BlackRock, you'll be expected to apply sound judgement and critical thinking to solve complex problems, adapt as the business evolves, and combine the curiosity to explore new approaches and technologies with the rigor to challenge the results. The scope of this role also includes the following responsibilities:

  • Build new features end-to-end, from concept and design through production deployment and support.
  • Develop and maintain scalable backend services using Python and .NET, and create intuitive frontend experiences using React and TypeScript.
  • Take ownership of components within a Software as a Service (SaaS) platform, including production monitoring, operational support, and incident resolution in cloud environments.
  • Apply information security principles throughout software design, development, testing, and deployment activities.
  • Contribute to engineering excellence through Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD), automated testing, code reviews, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Collaborate closely with product, engineering, and business stakeholders to deliver high-quality solutions that meet client and business needs.
  • Contribute to the design and evolution of cloud-native, distributed systems and modern application architectures.

Your experience

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Organizational Sciences, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Demonstrated experience developing backend applications with Python and .NET, together with frontend development using modern frameworks such as React and TypeScript.
  • Strong understanding of software engineering principles, Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) concepts, and best practices, combined with strong analytical, problem-solving, and prioritization skills.
  • Experience designing, building, and integrating APIs using Representational State Transfer (REST), gRPC, and modern microservices-based architectures.
  • Experience working within existing codebases and contributing to the deployment of cloud-native applications.
  • Strong communication skills in English and an interest in understanding business and product domains; experience in financial services is beneficial.
  • Familiarity with data technologies such as Microsoft SQL Server, MongoDB, and Snowflake.

Nice to have

  • Experience with Java development.
  • Experience with GraphQL APIs and application integrations.
  • Exposure to Amazon Web Services (AWS).
  • Familiarity with enterprise-grade container orchestration platforms supporting declarative infrastructure and horizontal scaling.
  • Familiarity with modern DevOps practices and cloud-native engineering approaches.

Our benefits

To help you stay energized, engaged and inspired, we offer a wide range of employee benefits including: retirement investment and tools designed to help you in building a sound financial future; access to education reimbursement; comprehensive resources to support your physical health and emotional well-being; family support programs; and Flexible Time Off (FTO) so you can relax, recharge and be there for the people you care about.

Our hybrid work model

BlackRock’s hybrid work model is designed to enable a culture of collaboration and apprenticeship that enriches the experience of our employees, while supporting flexibility for all. Employees are currently required to work at least 4 days in the office per week, with the flexibility to work from home 1 day a week. Some business groups may require more time in the office due to their roles and responsibilities. We remain focused on increasing the impactful moments that arise when we work together in person – aligned with our commitment to performance and innovation. As a new joiner, you can count on this hybrid model to accelerate your learning and onboarding experience here at BlackRock.


Guidance on AI use for candidates


At BlackRock, AI has long been part of how we work – enhancing decision-making, improving operations, and helping us deliver better outcomes for clients. We encourage candidates to use AI thoughtfully to learn, prepare, and work more effectively; but during our interview process, we want to focus on getting to know you through your own experiences, thinking, and judgment. To support you, we’ve provided guidance on when and how to use AI during our hiring process so you can approach each step with confidence and showcase your best self.


About BlackRock


At BlackRock, we are all connected by one mission: to help more and more people experience financial well-being. Our clients, and the people they serve, are saving for retirement, paying for their children’s educations, buying homes and starting businesses. Their investments also help to strengthen the global economy: support businesses small and large; finance infrastructure projects that connect and power cities; and facilitate innovations that drive progress.


This mission would not be possible without our smartest investment – the one we make in our employees. It’s why we’re dedicated to creating an environment where our colleagues feel welcomed, valued and supported with networks, benefits and development opportunities to help them thrive.


To learn more about BlackRock, please visit Careers.BlackRock.com. We also encourage you to get to know us on LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube, X, and TikTok.


BlackRock is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to age, disability, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation and other protected characteristics at law.

title: Principal Scientist - Induced Proximity Medicinal Chemistry
description:
Career Category

Scientific

Job Description

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.


Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.


Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.


Principal Scientist - Induced Proximity Medicinal Chemistry


What you will do.

Let's do this. Let's change the world. In this vital role, you will be part of an innovative Medicinal Chemistry group, designing and advancing small-molecule induced-proximity medicines for potential clinical development. You will apply strong hands-on synthetic and medicinal chemistry expertise to PROTACs, molecular glue degraders, and other proximity-based modalities, integrating molecular design with an understanding of ternary-complex biology, target engagement, protein degradation or functional modulation, and drug-like properties. This is an onsite laboratory position at our Thousand Oaks site.


Responsibilities:

  • Design, synthesize, purify, and characterize high-quality small molecules across relevant proximity modalities, including heterobifunctional degraders, molecular glues, and emerging targeted-chimera approaches; apply sound strategy to target ligands, E3 ligase or recruiter ligands, linker architecture, attachment vectors, and property-modulating elements.
  • Devise and implement state-of-the-art medicinal chemistry research for induced-proximity programs, including detailed experimental plans, decision criteria, and expected results, from hit finding through development-candidate nomination.
  • Lead hypothesis-driven SAR and structure-property-activity relationships that integrate potency, degradation or functional response, selectivity, cooperativity, ternary-complex behavior, target engagement, permeability, solubility, metabolic stability, pharmacokinetics, and developability.
  • Collaborate closely with chemical biology, structural biology, biophysics, proteomics, cell biology, DMPK, safety, translational sciences, and computational chemistry colleagues to interpret complex datasets, resolve mechanism and selectivity questions, and guide molecular design.
  • Develop practical strategies to address modality-specific medicinal chemistry challenges, including molecular weight and polarity, linker conformational control, permeability and efflux, oral exposure, tissue distribution, E3-ligase expression and engagement, neosubstrate risk, hook effect, and durable pharmacology.
  • Maintain awareness of the induced-proximity landscape, including emerging proximity mechanisms, E3 ligases and other recruiters, chemical biology tools, assays, relevant publications, and patent activity; identify opportunities that strengthen the portfolio and platform.
  • Provide technical guidance and mentorship to scientists, research associates, and external chemistry partners; ensure rigorous experimental design, data integrity, documentation, safe laboratory practice, and timely execution.
  • Generate scientific results that support high-impact publications, patents, conference presentations, and productive external collaborations.
  • We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The qualified professional we seek is a Principal Scientist with these qualifications.

Basic Qualifications:

Doctorate degree and 2 years of scientific experience, or

Master's degree and 5 years of scientific experience, or

Bachelor's degree and 7 years of scientific experience


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Doctorate degree in organic chemistry, medicinal chemistry, chemical biology, or a closely related discipline, with 6+ years of experience in synthetic organic and medicinal chemistry.
  • Demonstrated experience designing, synthesizing, and optimizing induced-proximity medicines, particularly PROTACs and/or molecular glue degraders; experience with additional targeted-chimera modalities, is highly desirable.
  • Strong command of modern medicinal and synthetic chemistry approaches, including the efficient preparation of complex, highly functionalized small molecules and the use of parallel synthesis, route design, purification, and analytical characterization to accelerate SAR.
  • Ability to translate integrated biology, biophysical, biochemical, proteomics, cellular, DMPK, and in vivo data into actionable compound-design hypotheses; familiarity with degradation metrics such as DC50, Dmax, kinetics, selectivity, and exposure-response relationships.
  • Deep understanding of discovery disciplines relevant to induced proximity, including chemical biology, structural biology, biophysics, cellular pharmacology, DMPK, safety, and translational science.
  • Extensive record of impactful drug-discovery accomplishments, demonstrated through patent inventorship, peer-reviewed publications, scientific presentations, and successful cross-functional collaboration.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, sound scientific judgment, a collaborative leadership style, and the ability to mentor colleagues and influence decisions across a matrixed organization.

What you can expect from us

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

title: Vice President, EMEA Employee Compliance Advisory
location: BU3-Budapest-GTC White House, Vaci ut 47, District XIII, Budapest
description:
About this role

Your team


Employee Compliance sits within BlackRock's Legal & Compliance function and is responsible for the framework governing employees' personal activities. The EMEA Employee Compliance Advisory team provides practical advice and guidance on Employee Compliance requirements and supports the identification, assessment, and management of employee conflicts. The team operates within a globally consistent framework while providing regionally attuned engagement, local regulatory interpretation, and judgment-based review across EMEA.

Your role and impact


As Vice President, EMEA Employee Compliance Advisory, you will provide clear, practical, risk-based advice across the region, with a particular focus on personal trading, private investments, Outside Business Activities (OBA), and Gifts & Entertainment (G&E). You will manage complex, sensitive, and higher-risk matters while providing high-touch support to the EMEA executive population. You will apply sound judgment and discretion, help ensure advice and outcomes are consistent and well documented, and use insights from advisory activity to identify emerging risks and recurring themes that can strengthen the broader Employee Compliance program.

Your responsibilities


In every role at BlackRock, you'll be expected to apply sound judgement and critical thinking to solve complex problems, adapt as the business evolves, and combine the curiosity to explore new approaches and technologies with the rigor to challenge the results. The scope of this role also includes the following responsibilities:

  • Provide practical, risk-based Employee Compliance advice across EMEA, managing employee queries and submissions relating to personal trading, private investments, OBA, and G&E, and escalating novel or judgment-based matters appropriately.
  • Issue non-compliance notifications and support targeted OBA and G&E campaigns, training, and employee communications across the region.
  • Review policy exceptions, escalations, and pre-clearance requests across personal trading, private investments, OBA, and G&E, ensuring decisions and conditions are appropriately documented.
  • Provide high-touch support to the EMEA executive population and engage effectively with executive assistants, family offices, financial advisers, and brokers while maintaining appropriate policy standards and discretion.
  • Deliver training and communications for functions supporting executives and assist in resolving legacy records and data issues.
  • Operate the regional advisory hotline, support regulatory and audit activity, and contribute to regional training and local policy implementation.
  • Maintain connectivity with regional Chief Compliance Officers (CCOs) and partner across Program Operations, Advisory Compliance, Information Barriers/Control Room, Legal, and Human Resources, using advisory activity and case trends to inform policies, procedures, controls, training, and communications.

Your experience


  • Significant relevant experience in Compliance, Legal, Risk, or a related control function within financial services, ideally within asset management, investment management, or banking.
  • Strong subject-matter expertise in employee compliance and personal conflicts, including personal trading, private investments, Outside Business Activities (OBA), and Gifts & Entertainment (G&E).
  • Strong understanding of regulatory and conflicts-of-interest considerations relating to employees' personal activities, Codes of Ethics, and EMEA conduct and personal-account-dealing requirements.
  • Proven ability to assess complex, sensitive, and judgment-based matters, apply sound risk judgment, make well-reasoned decisions, and escalate appropriately.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to translate complex requirements into clear, practical guidance and constructively challenge stakeholders at different levels of the organization.
  • Experience working across compliance functions and centralized operations, combined with the discretion, organization, and relationship-management skills required to support senior executives and their representatives.
  • A bachelor's degree or equivalent experience; an advanced legal, compliance, or related professional qualification is advantageous. Experience with private markets or private-investment reviews would also be beneficial.


The salary range for Hungary is 16400000 - 26700000 HUF

Additionally, employees are eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, and benefits including healthcare, leave benefits, and retirement benefits. BlackRock operates a pay-for-performance compensation philosophy and your total compensation may vary based on role, location, and firm, department and individual performance.

Our benefits

To help you stay energized, engaged and inspired, we offer a wide range of employee benefits including: retirement investment and tools designed to help you in building a sound financial future; access to education reimbursement; comprehensive resources to support your physical health and emotional well-being; family support programs; and Flexible Time Off (FTO) so you can relax, recharge and be there for the people you care about.

Our hybrid work model

BlackRock’s hybrid work model is designed to enable a culture of collaboration and apprenticeship that enriches the experience of our employees, while supporting flexibility for all. Employees are currently required to work at least 4 days in the office per week, with the flexibility to work from home 1 day a week. Some business groups may require more time in the office due to their roles and responsibilities. We remain focused on increasing the impactful moments that arise when we work together in person – aligned with our commitment to performance and innovation. As a new joiner, you can count on this hybrid model to accelerate your learning and onboarding experience here at BlackRock.


Guidance on AI use for candidates


At BlackRock, AI has long been part of how we work – enhancing decision-making, improving operations, and helping us deliver better outcomes for clients. We encourage candidates to use AI thoughtfully to learn, prepare, and work more effectively; but during our interview process, we want to focus on getting to know you through your own experiences, thinking, and judgment. To support you, we’ve provided guidance on when and how to use AI during our hiring process so you can approach each step with confidence and showcase your best self.


About BlackRock


At BlackRock, we are all connected by one mission: to help more and more people experience financial well-being. Our clients, and the people they serve, are saving for retirement, paying for their children’s educations, buying homes and starting businesses. Their investments also help to strengthen the global economy: support businesses small and large; finance infrastructure projects that connect and power cities; and facilitate innovations that drive progress.


This mission would not be possible without our smartest investment – the one we make in our employees. It’s why we’re dedicated to creating an environment where our colleagues feel welcomed, valued and supported with networks, benefits and development opportunities to help them thrive.


To learn more about BlackRock, please visit Careers.BlackRock.com. We also encourage you to get to know us on LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube, X, and TikTok.

description:
ABOUT US

The nonprofit YMCA of Western North Carolina strengthens local communities through youth development, healthy living, and social responsibility. Founded in 1889, we engage more than 100,000 people – regardless of age, income, or background – to nurture the potential of children and teens, improve the region’s health and well-being, and provide opportunities to give back and support the community. We do this through seven YMCAs, dozens of program sites, and YMCA Camp Watia. As the state’s largest provider of licensed school-age childcare, we give more than 1,000 children a day the opportunity to learn, grow, and thrive. We are made up of people of all ages, from all backgrounds, working side by side to ensure that everyone can reach their full potential with dignity. Thus, we are “For All”. Our core values are caring, honesty, respect, and responsibility, and they guide everything we do. We are committed to being an organization that exposes and addresses social constraints that limit and/or negatively affect all humans from all walks of life. We recruit staff who are passionate about giving back to the community, helping people, and upholding our core values. For more information, please visit .

ABOUT THE ROLE

As the Group Exercise Instructor, you will be responsible for delivering exceptional service to all members, guests, and program participants. You will be responsible for completing the performance of implemented wellness strategies; this includes delivering thoughtful, engaging, safe, effective, and enjoyable Group Exercise classes to YMCA members and guests.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

  • Teaches and leads group exercise classes in a way that supports the recruitment of new members and retention of existing members to meet association goals.
  • Maintains group fitness equipment, rooms, and storage areas.

title: Global Marketing & Digital Wealth Delivery Manager(Fixed-term)
description:
About this role

The Team:

The Global Marketing & Digital Wealth organization at BlackRock is a forward-looking, globally connected team at the center of the firm’s most high-impact priorities. We are architects of growth, working across functions and markets to unlock opportunities and accelerate outcomes for the business. In collaboration with both internal and external partners, we design the conditions for success—delivering next-generation campaigns, brand platforms, communications, training, and client experiences. Our work is powered by world-class centers of excellence spanning content strategy, research & analytics, and digital platforms & experiences.


Within Global Marketing & Digital Wealth, the Global Digital team owns and transforms BlackRock’s client-facing digital properties—including BlackRock.com, iShares.com, and Advisor Center—as well as our email marketing channels. The team brings together product, design, engineering, and digital expertise to create connected, personalized experiences that help clients discover, understand, and engage with BlackRock.


Role and Impact:

We believe the future of ETF distribution is digital. As ETF adoption accelerates around the world, we have a unique opportunity to shape the future of the investment industry. We are on a mission to transform iShares.com, to inspire and champion investor progress by creating the most trusted, valued, and relevant digital experience.


We’re looking for a Delivery Manager (maternity cover) to join our Digital Experiences team to support the development and build of the iShares.com websites. The successful candidate will adapt quickly to new circumstances as they arise, working within a multi-disciplined development team to guide growth, refine processes, and enable the team to build and run outstanding products using agile methodologies. This role reports directly to the Delivery Lead, based in Budapest. The Budapest office is our primary work location, and all employees must work from the office at least four days per week.


Responsibilities:

  • Work within a multi-disciplined development team supporting the team, guiding growth, and refining processes, enabling the team to build and run outstanding product using agile methodologies.
  • Remove impediments and blockers on a day-to-day basis.
  • Work with the Product Manager and team to define the roadmap of the product delivery.
  • Lead the collaborative planning process for each sprint, helping the team to prioritise and self-organise around the work, keeping in mind their capability and capacity.
  • Facilitate the team’s meetings (Planning, Daily Stand-Up, Refinement, Retrospective, etc.) as well as other workshops as needed by the team and business.
  • Guide, mentor, and coach team members and partners on agile and scrum principles and practices.
  • Be responsible for the development process, guiding the team through continuous improvements and release cycles.
  • Coordinate the release preparation and release process.
  • Create, collate, and understand progress metrics with the team.
  • Engage with the Delivery Management community, sharing practices, developing each other, and experimenting in a safe space.

Core Skills:

  • Excellent people and communication skills.
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills.
  • A calm, dedicated, and optimistic individual.
  • Ability to work independently.
  • Coaching-oriented—develops teams and partners in agile ways of working.

Qualifications:

  • 1–3 years as a Scrum Master working with software development teams delivering complex projects.
  • Experienced in project management and/or facilitation, coaching, and mentoring.
  • Extensive use of JIRA, Confluence, Azure, Miro, Conceptboard, or other online collaboration and management tools.


The salary range for Hungary is 13400000 - 20100000 HUF

Additionally, employees are eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, and benefits including healthcare, leave benefits, and retirement benefits. BlackRock operates a pay-for-performance compensation philosophy and your total compensation may vary based on role, location, and firm, department and individual performance.

Our benefits

To help you stay energized, engaged and inspired, we offer a wide range of employee benefits including: retirement investment and tools designed to help you in building a sound financial future; access to education reimbursement; comprehensive resources to support your physical health and emotional well-being; family support programs; and Flexible Time Off (FTO) so you can relax, recharge and be there for the people you care about.

Our hybrid work model

BlackRock’s hybrid work model is designed to enable a culture of collaboration and apprenticeship that enriches the experience of our employees, while supporting flexibility for all. Employees are currently required to work at least 4 days in the office per week, with the flexibility to work from home 1 day a week. Some business groups may require more time in the office due to their roles and responsibilities. We remain focused on increasing the impactful moments that arise when we work together in person – aligned with our commitment to performance and innovation. As a new joiner, you can count on this hybrid model to accelerate your learning and onboarding experience here at BlackRock.


Guidance on AI use for candidates


At BlackRock, AI has long been part of how we work – enhancing decision-making, improving operations, and helping us deliver better outcomes for clients. We encourage candidates to use AI thoughtfully to learn, prepare, and work more effectively; but during our interview process, we want to focus on getting to know you through your own experiences, thinking, and judgment. To support you, we’ve provided guidance on when and how to use AI during our hiring process so you can approach each step with confidence and showcase your best self.


About BlackRock


At BlackRock, we are all connected by one mission: to help more and more people experience financial well-being. Our clients, and the people they serve, are saving for retirement, paying for their children’s educations, buying homes and starting businesses. Their investments also help to strengthen the global economy: support businesses small and large; finance infrastructure projects that connect and power cities; and facilitate innovations that drive progress.


This mission would not be possible without our smartest investment – the one we make in our employees. It’s why we’re dedicated to creating an environment where our colleagues feel welcomed, valued and supported with networks, benefits and development opportunities to help them thrive.


To learn more about BlackRock, please visit Careers.BlackRock.com. We also encourage you to get to know us on LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube, X, and TikTok.


BlackRock is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to age, disability, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation and other protected characteristics at law.

description:
APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS:

  • CURRENT PENN STATE STUDENT (not employed previously at the university) and seeking employment with Penn State, please login to Workday to complete the student application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday.

This position is funded for 1 year(s); continuation past 1 year(s) will be based on university need, performance, and/or availability of funding.

​

POSITION SPECIFICS​

The Cancer Institute at the Penn State College in Hershey, PA is seeking a Compliance Specialist. This position involves ensuring that the quality of research in the PSCI CTO is pristine in terms of compliance with all regulations including those from our PSCI IRB, other IRB's, FDA, sponsor's obligations etc. This applies both to active ongoing clinical trials and also to the development/startup of new clinical trials in the office. The latter (startup of new trials) are absolutely necessary to increasing clinical trials activity and help for our patients; however this process is fraught with potential error and risk management without leadership from high quality compliance specialist.

MINIMUM EDUCATION, WORK EXPERIENCE & REQUIRED CERTIFICATIONS

Bachelor's Degree
1+ years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience accepted
Required Certifications:
None

- Manage all regulatory and compliance aspects of a portfolio of cancer clinical trials, including ensuring that the protocol investigators and staff are fully certified and trained for the trials, ensuring that they are complying with good clinical practice and following the protocol, that continuing reviews and reportable new information are performed on time, and adverse events are promptly and accurately reported. Also manage study amendments, action letters and other changes to the protocol. The primary difference between this position and Compliance specialist-professional is that the number and complexity of active trials being managed will be greater.


- Act as a study startup coordinator for multiple new trials, from the process of ensuring that CDA's are appropriately executed between sponsors and investigators/Penn state, all the way up to ensuring that congruence of all documents is perfect and the study ready for activation. This involves very frequent communication with sponsor, investigators, COM offices of budget, legal, contracts, IRB and related committees (e.g. biosafety, radiation safety), as well as PSCI specific committees including protocol scientific review committee and data safety committee. The primary difference between this position and Compliance specialist-professional is that the number and complexity of active trials being managed will be greater, and will include some work in the phase I arena.


- Serve as a liaison among the PI, study team (investigators and research staff) and other stakeholders including people from other departments involved in the study but are not part of the official study team (e.g. radiology, pathology et al.). Manage training logs and other documentation required.


- Participation in disease team meetings including preparation of reports/slides for meetings. Compile information from meetings, particularly action items, and communicate them to stakeholders.

BACKGROUND CHECKS/CLEARANCES

Employment with the University will require successful completion of background check(s) in accordance with University policies.

Penn State does not sponsor or take over sponsorship of a staff employment Visa. Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S.

In addition to comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, employees enjoy robust retirement plans and substantial paid time off which includes holidays, vacation and sick time. description:
Organization Overview, Mission, Vision, and Values

Our mission is to improve the health of people in the communities we serve through compassionate, high-quality care, prevention, and wellness education. Washington Regional Medical System is a community-owned, locally governed, non-profit health care system located in Northwest Arkansas in the heart of Fayetteville, which is consistently ranked among the Best Places to live in the country. Our 425-bed medical center has been named the #1 hospital in Arkansas for five consecutive years by U.S. News & World Report. We employ 3,200+ team members and serve the region with over 40 clinic locations, the region’s only Level II trauma center, and five Centers of Excellence - the Washington Regional J.B. Hunt Transport Services Neuroscience Institute; Washington Regional Walker Heart Institute; Washington Regional Women and Infants Center; Washington Regional Total Joint Center; and Washington Regional Pat Walker Center for Seniors.

Position Summary

The role of the Sterile Processing Technician reports to the Sterile Processing Department Manager. This position is responsible for the decontamination and sterilization of all hospital instruments.

Essential Position Responsibilities

  • Ensure proper protocol is followed for the decontamination of instruments
  • Assemble and sterilize instruments ensuring proper sterilization technique
  • Catalog and re-stock crash carts and urology carts
  • Ensure proper High-Level Disinfection (HLD) of semi-critical items is performed
  • Assemble case carts as needed for surgical case
  • Properly open and ensure stock is stored appropriately

title: Payments Business Risk Management Executive, Senior Vice President
description:
Who we are looking for

We are looking for a Payments Business Risk Management Executive, Senior Vice President to lead and steward the first-line risk and control agenda across the firm’s global Payments business.

This senior executive will operate as a strategic partner to the Head of Payments and the Head of Business Controls & Enterprise Resiliency, with a dual reporting relationship that ensures close alignment between Payments business priorities and the firm’s broader risk, control and resiliency agenda.

The successful candidate will bring deep experience in financial services, payments and/or business risk management, combined with the executive presence and commercial judgment required to influence senior leaders across a complex global organization.

Why this role is important to us

Payments represents a critical component of the firm’s global operating environment, supporting high-volume, time-sensitive and highly regulated activities across multiple markets, platforms and clients.

As the Payments business continues to modernize its platforms, operating models and capabilities, this role will ensure that risk management and controls are embedded into business strategy, transformation and day-to-day execution.

The role will provide senior first-line risk leadership across enterprise-wide Payments while partnering closely with Business Controls & Enterprise Resiliency, Risk, Compliance, Technology, Product and Operations.

What you will be responsible for

Business Risk & Control Leadership

  • Lead and steward the first-line risk and control agenda for enterprise-wide Payments globally, ensuring risks are identified, assessed, monitored, mitigated and appropriately escalated.
  • Serve as the senior Business Risk Management partner to the Head of Payments, providing strategic advice and constructive challenge on business, operational and transformation priorities.
  • Ensure appropriate risk, controls and governance for this critical business service and related processes across the firm
  • Maintain a comprehensive view of the Payments risk profile across platforms, products, processes and geographies.
  • Drive consistent and sustainable risk and control practices across the global Payments organization.
  • Establish effective governance, reporting, issue management and escalation mechanisms for material risks and control matters.

Transformation, Resiliency & Regulatory

  • Provide risk leadership and challenge across Payments transformation, including technology modernization, automation, platform change and operating model redesign.
  • Partner with Product, Technology and Operations to ensure risk and control requirements are embedded in new capabilities and material change programs.
  • Strengthen operational resilience across critical Payments services and ensure appropriate consideration of technology, process and third-party dependencies.
  • Lead first-line engagement on significant issues, including root-cause analysis, remediation and sustainable risk reduction.
  • Partner with Risk, Compliance, Legal and Internal Audit and support regulatory examinations, audits and other reviews relating to Payments.
  • Represent the Payments risk and control agenda in senior governance and risk forums.

Leadership & Culture

  • Promote strong first-line ownership and an effective risk and control culture throughout Payments.
  • Build trusted relationships across business, product, technology and control functions and influence outcomes in a highly matrixed global organization.
  • Lead and develop a high-performing Payments Business Risk Management team, building strong capabilities, accountability and succession
  • Play a key leadership role in Business Controls and resiliency organisation, developing best practices, innovation and standards
  • Act as a change leader, balancing appropriate risk management with the commercial and strategic objectives of the Payments business.

What we value

At Senior Vice President level, we are looking for an established leader who combines strong risk and control expertise with deep business understanding and executive influence.

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

  • Significant leadership experience in financial services, with experience across payments, transaction banking, banking operations, operational risk or first-line business risk management.
  • Deep understanding of operational and non-financial risk, controls, governance, issue management and remediation.
  • Strong understanding of complex, high-volume and time-critical payment environments.
  • Experience supporting major technology, operational or business transformation programs within regulated financial services.
  • Proven ability to partner with and constructively challenge senior executives while maintaining a pragmatic and commercially focused approach.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a dual-reporting, highly matrixed global organization.
  • Strong understanding of regulatory expectations and operational resilience within financial services.
  • Experience engaging with senior Risk, Compliance, Audit and regulatory stakeholders.
  • Excellent executive communication, influencing and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead through complexity, ambiguity and significant organizational change.

Qualifications & Experience

  • 15+ years of relevant financial services experience, including significant senior leadership experience.
  • Experience in Payments, Treasury Services, Transaction Banking, Banking Operations, Business Risk Management or related areas strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience leading risk and control agendas across complex global businesses or platforms.
  • Experience providing risk leadership for significant business and technology transformation.
  • Strong people leadership and talent development experience.
  • Graduate degree or equivalent professional experience; relevant risk, finance or business qualifications are advantageous.

$225 000 - $337 500 Annual

title: Care Coordination Center Representative
description:
The Care Coordination Center will provide a centralized, consistent, and patient-focused approach to handling incoming calls and clinical inquiries for the practice. They will use clinical judgment within the scope of their license and established practice protocols to determine the appropriate response to patient needs and ensure timely communication with providers and clinical staff.

Position Overview: The Care Coordination Center is responsible for coordinating and managing the day-to-day operations of the Call Coordination Center, serving as a central point of contact for patients. This position combines medical and nursing knowledge with high-level patient communication, telephone triage, scheduling, prescription refill coordination, and administrative support. This position will work closely with LPN’s and MA’s.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Patient Calls & Call Center Operations

Answer and manage incoming patient calls in a professional, courteous, and timely manner.

Serve as the primary point of contact for patients calling the practice.

Identify the reason for each call and appropriately address, route, or escalate the patient's needs.

Provide patients with clear information regarding office procedures, appointments, medications, and other appropriate non-diagnostic questions.

Document all patient interactions accurately in the electronic medical record (EMR).

Maintain a high level of customer service and professionalism with every patient interaction.

Assist in establishing and maintaining Care Coordination Center workflows, protocols, and standards.

Nurse Line / Clinical Patient Questions

Manage the centralized nurse line and respond to patient clinical questions within the scope of practice and established protocols.

Obtain appropriate information from patients to understand their concerns.

Provide approved nursing guidance and patient education as directed by practice protocols.

Identify urgent or potentially concerning symptoms and appropriately escalate calls to a provider or clinical staff.

Communicate patient concerns and messages to physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, or other appropriate clinical personnel.

Follow established protocols for urgent, same-day, and routine patient concerns.

Ensure appropriate follow-up and documentation of clinical telephone encounters.

Scheduling & Appointment Management

Schedule new and established patient appointments.

Reschedule and cancel appointments as requested if appropriate.

Assist patients in determining the appropriate appointment type, provider, and timeframe based on established office guidelines.

Coordinate urgent and same-day appointments when appropriate.

Communicate appointment information and instructions to patients.

Assist with managing appointment-related calls and patient questions.

Prescription Refill Management

Receive and process medication refill requests according to established practice protocols.

Review refill requests for required information and route requests appropriately.

Communicate with providers and clinical staff regarding refill requests requiring review or authorization.

Communicate with pharmacies and patients when necessary.

Document prescription-related communications accurately in the EMR.

Escalate refill requests that require clinical review or provider intervention.

Administrative & Document Management

Upload incoming faxes into the appropriate electronic medical records or document management system.

Scan and index medical records and other documents accurately.

Route documents, faxes, and clinical information to the appropriate office, provider, or staff member.

Assist with maintaining organized and accurate electronic patient records.

Monitor incoming documentation to ensure timely processing and appropriate follow-up.

Support individual practice offices with centralized administrative and clinical communication needs.

Obtain prior-authorization for medications and/or testing for procedures.

Communication & Care Coordination

Serve as a communication link between patients, providers, nurses, medical assistants, front-office staff, pharmacies, and other members of the healthcare team.

Ensure messages are complete, accurate, and directed to the appropriate individual or department.

Follow up on outstanding patient messages when required.

Help reduce unnecessary transfers and improve the overall patient experience by resolving issues whenever possible at the Care Coordination Center level.

Maintain confidentiality and comply with HIPAA and all applicable organizational policies and procedures.

Other duties as assigned.

title: REFERRAL TRACKING COORDINATOR I (TEMP - 3 Months)
description:
The Referral Tracking Coordinator (RTC) is responsible for the processing of all medical referrals initiated by NEMS PCPs from start to finish, which includes verifying patient’s eligibility and coverage information from various insurance plans, requesting prior authorizations from health plan(s), communicating with hospitals and specialty providers’ offices to follow up referral requests, scheduling appointments, confirm completion of visits by obtaining consultation notes, documenting progress in Epic EHR system to keep PCPs and care team informed.

The RTC-I is responsible for the tracking of all the in-progress medical referrals, perform additional needed activities to ensure referrals initiated by PCPs are followed through according to TAT (Turnaround Time) requirement.

This position requires good communication and public relations skills to build rapport relationship with counterpart staff at external specialist offices and hospitals to facilitate a smooth close-the-loop process. The RTC Coordinator will work collaboratively with NEMS clinical team, external provider/vendor offices and hospital staff to promote workflow efficiency and team performance.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

  • Timely processing of medical referrals for all insurances, including Medi-Cal, Medicare, private insurance, self-pay, etc.
  • Obtain clinical information relevant to the patient’s referral and submit a complete packet of referral documents to the external provider’s office to avoid delays in patient care.
  • Track referral status and obtain consultation reports/results to close the referral loop.
  • Follow-up on the outstanding referrals report and contact patients to determine if patients still need/want the requested service.
  • Assist patients with contacting external provider offices or agencies to schedule appointments for the referred services.
  • Provide patients with accurate information regarding the referral, including specialty type, name of the specialty provider, address, phone number, and a copy of the referral, if appropriate.
  • Triage inquiries on referral status and communicate timely with the PCP care team if additional information is needed to process the referral.
  • Enter all referral related activities and communications in the patent’s Electronic Medical Record, including notes and any relevant information as it relates to the referral.
  • Performs other job duties as required by manager/supervisor.

description:

  • CURRENT PENN STATE STUDENT (not employed previously at the university) and seeking employment with Penn State, please login to Workday to complete the student application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday.

  • If you are NOT a current employee or student, please click “Apply” and complete the application process for external applicants.

Approval of remote and hybrid work is not guaranteed regardless of work location. For additional information on remote work at Penn State, see Notice to Out of State Applicants.

This position is funded for 12 months; continuation past 12 months will be based on university need, performance, and/or availability of funding.

​

POSITION SPECIFICS​

The Development, Risk and Resilience Lab, headed by Dr. Rina D. Eiden, and the REPEAT lab, headed by Dr. Emily Ansell, are seeking a full-time Human Research Technologist.

The Human Research Technologist will work on an NIH-funded longitudinal study on the role of maternal pre-postnatal substance use and co-occurring risks on parent-adolescent relationships and adolescent/young adult outcomes.

This is a continuation of a multi-method, longitudinal study of tobacco- and cannabis-exposed children and their mothers recruited in the 1st trimester of pregnancy.


The current phase of the study will examine social and emotional outcomes in adolescence/young adulthood including health experiences and risk behaviors, the parent-child relationship, social skills, and peer relationships.

Assessments will take place with families at multiple developmental stages, from early adolescence through young adulthood.

This work will take advantage of the University’s broad resources, including the Child Study Center.


Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Recruiting, scheduling appointments for, and maintaining contact with parents and adolescents/young adults through email, text messages, and phone calls
  • Conducting data collection activities on Zoom with adolescents and parents
  • Conducting Timeline Follow Back interviews with adolescents and parents
  • Collect and process EMA (ecological momentary assessment) surveys
  • Tracking EMA survey compliance of all enrolled participants
  • Coding observational assessments of parent-adolescent interactions

Data collection methods include observational assessments and online surveys, observational and physiological data, and ecological momentary assessments with young adults.

After training, various software and applications will be utilized. This includes Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint; R; and SPSS.


Important Note: This position requires a flexible schedule to include working some evenings and weekends, primarily to accommodate the availability of participating families.


Qualifications:

It is highly preferred that candidates have at least one year of relevant experience in research with families and/or adolescents/young adults/parents.

Additional Preferred Qualifications (one or more):

  • Research experience with family-based assessments
  • Experience with parent and adolescent interviews
  • Experience with observational data collection
  • Excellent organizational and interpersonal skills
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills

MINIMUM EDUCATION, WORK EXPERIENCE & REQUIRED CERTIFICATIONS

Associate Degree
No prior relevant work experience required; previous relevant work experience accepted in lieu of education.
Required Certifications:
None

A Bachelor’s degree in Psychology or related field is also preferred.

Applicants must upload a cover letter of interest, highlighting relevant skills, and a CV/resume.

Questions regarding the position may be addressed to Dr. Rina Eiden at rina.eiden@psu.edu

The College of the Liberal Arts is supportive of flexible work arrangements when aligned with the ability to meet the needs of the unit and the essential duties of the position. Questions related to flexible work should be directed to the hiring manager during the interview process.

This position requires the following clearances in addition to applicable background checks: PA State Police Criminal Background Check, PA Child Abuse History Clearance Form, and Federal (FBI) Fingerprint Criminal Background Check.

Penn State does not sponsor or take over sponsorship of a staff employment Visa. Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S.

title: Payments Business Risk Management Executive, Senior Vice President
description:
Who we are looking for

We are looking for a Payments Business Risk Management Executive, Senior Vice President to lead and steward the first-line risk and control agenda across the firm’s global Payments business.

This senior executive will operate as a strategic partner to the Head of Payments and the Head of Business Controls & Enterprise Resiliency, with a dual reporting relationship that ensures close alignment between Payments business priorities and the firm’s broader risk, control and resiliency agenda.

The successful candidate will bring deep experience in financial services, payments and/or business risk management, combined with the executive presence and commercial judgment required to influence senior leaders across a complex global organization.

Why this role is important to us

Payments represents a critical component of the firm’s global operating environment, supporting high-volume, time-sensitive and highly regulated activities across multiple markets, platforms and clients.

As the Payments business continues to modernize its platforms, operating models and capabilities, this role will ensure that risk management and controls are embedded into business strategy, transformation and day-to-day execution.

What you will be responsible for

Business Risk & Control Leadership

  • Lead and steward the first-line risk and control agenda for enterprise-wide Payments globally, ensuring risks are identified, assessed, monitored, mitigated and appropriately escalated.

  • Maintain a comprehensive view of the Payments risk profile across platforms, products, processes and geographies.
  • Drive consistent and sustainable risk and control practices across the global Payments organization.
  • Establish effective governance, reporting, issue management and escalation mechanisms for material risks and control matters.

Transformation, Resiliency & Regulatory

  • Provide risk leadership and challenge across Payments transformation, including technology modernization, automation, platform change and operating model redesign.
  • Partner with Product, Technology and Operations to ensure risk and control requirements are embedded in new capabilities and material change programs.
  • Strengthen operational resilience across critical Payments services and ensure appropriate consideration of technology, process and third-party dependencies.
  • Lead first-line engagement on significant issues, including root-cause analysis, remediation and sustainable risk reduction.
  • Partner with Risk, Compliance, Legal and Internal Audit and support regulatory examinations, audits and other reviews relating to Payments.
  • Represent the Payments risk and control agenda in senior governance and risk forums.

Leadership & Culture

  • Promote strong first-line ownership and an effective risk and control culture throughout Payments.

  • Play a key leadership role in Business Controls and resiliency organisation, developing best practices, innovation and standards
  • Act as a change leader, balancing appropriate risk management with the commercial and strategic objectives of the Payments business.

What we value

At Senior Vice President level, we are looking for an established leader who combines strong risk and control expertise with deep business understanding and executive influence.

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

  • Significant leadership experience in financial services, with experience across payments, transaction banking, banking operations, operational risk or first-line business risk management.
  • Deep understanding of operational and non-financial risk, controls, governance, issue management and remediation.

  • Proven ability to partner with and constructively challenge senior executives while maintaining a pragmatic and commercially focused approach.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a dual-reporting, highly matrixed global organization.
  • Strong understanding of regulatory expectations and operational resilience within financial services.
  • Experience engaging with senior Risk, Compliance, Audit and regulatory stakeholders.
  • Excellent executive communication, influencing and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead through complexity, ambiguity and significant organizational change.

Qualifications & Experience

  • 15+ years of relevant financial services experience, including significant senior leadership experience.

title: Strategic Planning Consultant
description:
The Lawyering Project is excited to launch our search for an experienced strategic planning partner to facilitate the development of our 2028-2033 strategic plan. This engagement will take place during February – July 2027 and the consultant will report to the Lawyering Project’s Executive Team.

Organizational Background

Founded in 2017, the Lawyering Project is a legal advocacy organization that blends traditional impact litigation with movement lawyering to promote reproductive health, rights, and justice throughout the United States. We have an all-remote staff that includes 24 full-time employees spread across the United States.

Laws that undermine reproductive health, rights, and justice deprive people of moral agency, rob us of control over our bodies, and compound other forms of oppression like racism, sexism, and poverty. Our mission is to eliminate these laws and the harmful impacts they have on people’s lives. We are especially focused on laws that limit the availability or affordability of abortion care; contribute to disparities in reproductive health outcomes; embody gender-based stereotypes; or discriminate against people based on their reproductive decisions.

We envision a society with laws that enable each of us to make decisions about intensely personal matters like sex, pregnancy, family, and healthcare based on our own beliefs and values, and ensure that we all have access to safe pregnancy care, safe abortion care, and safe communities for our families.

More information about the Lawyering Project is available on our website.

Project Background

Since its inception nearly a decade ago, the Lawyering Project has undergone significant growth in its staff size, programming, and overall organizational capacity, all while operating in a volatile political and legal landscape. We understand that, to realize our long-term vision for reproductive health, rights, and justice, we must continually assess our organizational strategy and impact. Energized by the organization’s growth, the exciting work being done by our clients and partners, and the growing need for legal services by those seeking, providing, and supporting abortion care, we are embarking on a strategic planning process to coincide with our tenth anniversary. Our goal for this process is to bring our creative, partner-driven approach to lawyering to bear on the challenges facing the repro movement nearly five years after the fall of Roe.

Project Scope of Work

  1. Design a process for the development of a five-year strategic plan that includes the following:
    • Robustly engaging with the Lawyering Project’s Board of Directors and staff;
    • Gathering input from key external stakeholders including clients, partners, and funders;
    • Evaluating the impact of the Lawyering Project’s current programs;
    • Assessing the strengths and weaknesses of the Lawyering Project's current operations; and
    • Providing the Lawyering Project’s Executive Team with periodic opportunities to review progress and offer feedback.
  2. Guide the Lawyering Project through the strategic planning process, taking the lead on meeting facilitation and data collection.
  3. Use the information and insights gathered to create a five-year strategic plan.
  4. Assist the Executive Team in creating metrics to assess progress under the strategic plan.

Requirements

Desired Consultant Expertise and Qualifications

  • Proven expertise in strategic planning for nonprofit organizations. Experience working with legal advocacy organizations is a plus.
  • Proven knowledge of the U.S. reproductive health, rights, and justice movement.
  • Demonstrated ability to facilitate group discussions and build alignment among stakeholders with differing perspectives.
  • Strong project management skills, especially the ability to complete deliverables on time and according to specifications.
  • Demonstrated commitment to JEDI (Justice, Equity, Diversity and Inclusion) and social justice.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills and readiness to work with a group of committed, talented, and enthusiastic individuals.

Budget

We are seeking bids of up to $40,000 for the entire project.

Submission Requirements

To apply, please submit the following materials by December 18, 2026:

  • A concise proposal detailing your approach to the project
  • An updated CV or resume
  • At least two client references from strategic planning projects
  • Any additional supporting materials that you would like us to consider

Our goal is to engage a consultant by January 31, 2027, and begin work on the project in early February.

  • Maintain the five-year financial plan and ensure alignment with approved strategic and operational priorities.
  • Establish planning assumptions, sensitivity ranges and clear version control for all budget and forecast submissions.
  • Allocate work effectively, review key outputs and maintain resilience across critical planning and reportingcycles.
  • Build strong working relationships across Finance, schools and HQ functions while maintaining independent financial challenge.

Management reporting and insight

  • Own monthly school, HQ and group management reporting, including actual versus budget and forecastanalysis.
  • Produce concise executive commentary explaining material variances, drivers, risks, opportunities and required management actions.
  • Develop dashboards and scorecards combining financial and non-financial measures, including enrolment, capacity utilisation, staffing ratios, revenue per student and cost per student.
  • Ensure reporting is accurate, consistent, decision-focused and delivered to agreed deadlines.
  • Respond to ad hoc analysis and group reporting requirements with clear assumptions and audit trails

Performance management and business partnering

  • Lead regular performance reviews with school and functional leaders, challenging results constructively and agreeing recovery or improvement actions.
  • Partner with business leaders on workforce planning, resource allocation, pricing, cost optimisation andoperating-model decisions.
  • Evaluate business cases, growth initiatives and operational investments through financial modelling, scenario analysis and post-investment review.
  • Identify portfolio-wide performance trends, benchmarks and opportunities to improve financial sustainability andoperational efficiency.
  • Track agreed actions, benefits and financial outcomes, escalating significant risks or delivery gaps to the CFO.

FP&A governance, systems and data

  • Define and maintain FP&A policies, calendars, templates, controls and approval requirements.
  • Maintain a single, controlled source of planning and reporting data, with documented ownership andreconciliation procedures.
  • Drive continuous improvement and automation of planning, reporting and analytical processes within the ERPand supporting tools.
  • Ensure models are robust, transparent, appropriately controlled and supported by documented assumptions.
  • Coordinate with Financial Control to ensure management information reconciles to the general ledger andapproved financial records.

Leadership:

  • Lead, coach and develop the FP&A team, setting clear objectives, service standards and development plans.
  • Allocate work effectively, review key outputs and maintain resilience across critical planning and reportingcycles.
  • Build strong working relationships across Finance, schools and HQ functions while maintaining independent financial challenge.

Corporate Finance and strategic investment

  • Lead financial evaluation of strategic growth opportunities, new schools, acquisitions, partnerships, capacity expansion and major investment initiatives.
  • Develop and review investment models, business cases, valuation analysis, sensitivity analysis and scenario assessments to support executive and Board decisions.
  • Identify medium- and long-term funding requirements arising from approved business plans, capital programmes and growth initiatives.
  • Support the CFO in evaluating external and intercompany funding options, including the financial implications,affordability and impact on cash flow and returns.
  • Prepare financial analysis and decision materials for Executive Leadership, Board and investment approvalforums.
  • Assess capital allocation priorities and provide recommendations based on strategic alignment, financial returns,risk and affordability.
  • Monitor the long-term financial performance and return profile of school assets and major investments against approved business cases.
  • Conduct post-investment reviews and track the delivery of approved financial benefits, assumptions andreturns.
  • Coordinate with Aldar Group Finance, advisers, lenders and relevant stakeholders on Corporate Financematters as required.
  • Establish and maintain appropriate Corporate Finance models, processes, controls, documentation and approval records.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business or a related discipline.
  • Professional accounting qualification such as ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CPA or CA strongly preferred; relevant master’s degreedesirable.

Minimum Experience:

  • Minimum 12 years of progressive finance experience, including at least 5 years leading FP&A, budgeting,forecasting or management reporting teams.
  • Demonstrable ownership of complex, multi-entity or multi-site budgeting, forecasting and management-reporting cycles.
  • Strong experience presenting financial performance, risks and recommendations to CFO and executive-level stakeholders.
  • Advanced financial modelling, scenario analysis and business-case evaluation experience.
  • Experience with ERP, planning and business-intelligence tools; education, services or other multi-site operatingenvironments preferred.
  • Experience supporting growth, transformation or performance-improvement programmes desirable.
  • Experience in investment appraisal, funding analysis, capital allocation, valuation or Corporate Finance projects.

Job Specific Knowledge & Skills:

  • Expert knowledge of FP&A disciplines, including driver-based planning, rolling forecasts, variance analysis, scenario modelling and long-range planning.
  • Strong understanding of the Income Statement, Balance Sheet and Cash Flow Statement, and the links between operational drivers and financial outcomes.
  • Advanced Excel and financial-modelling capability; able to review model logic, assumptions, controls andoutputs.
  • Strong data and systems orientation, with the ability to improve ERP, planning and business-intelligence reporting processes.
  • Commercial judgement and the confidence to challenge assumptions, influence senior stakeholders andconvert analysis into decisions.
  • Clear executive communication, including concise written commentary and presentation of complexinformation.
  • Strong people leadership, coaching, prioritisation and quality-review capability.
  • High standards of accuracy, ownership, confidentiality and deadline management.
  • Fluent written and spoken English; cultural sensitivity and effectiveness in a diverse stakeholder environment.
  • Strong knowledge of investment appraisal methods, including discounted cash flow, net present value, internal rate of return, payback analysis and sensitivity modelling.
  • Ability to evaluate funding requirements, capital allocation choices and the financial implications of strategic growth decisions.

Aldar Education is a family of world-class, child-centered, and innovative schools based in the UAE.
